## 2026-09-30 - Codex - Proposed class progression across tiers 1-6; coherence and Ironhide reference

Jacob asked how the 17 classes fit six tiers and change/disrupt gameplay coherently, suggesting Ironhide tower progression as a reference. Read the current locks, final class catalogue and latest shared log, including Claude's ArtLab handoff. Research/design discussion only. The following is a RECOMMENDATION FOR DISCUSSION, not a newly locked tier assignment or a claim of tested balance. DESIGN_LOCKS.md and both class JSON files remain unchanged.

Proposed first-unlock distribution: 4 + 4 + 3 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 17.
- Tier 1: Warden, Vanguard, Marksman, Medic (4 cumulative). Establish protection, initiating a fight, focused ranged damage and health recovery.
- Tier 2: Berserker, Skirmisher, Duelist, Trapper (8 cumulative). Offer aggression, mobile damage, timed counters and anticipatory route control.
- Tier 3: Recon, Herald, Chemist (11 cumulative). Coordinate target focus, sanity recovery and suppression as narrative encounters combine threats.
- Tier 4: Artillerist, Infiltrator (13 cumulative). Answer clusters and defended formations through area pressure or a flank.
- Tier 5: Field Engineer, Binder (15 cumulative). Establish temporary firing positions and move eligible enemies into existing attacks/control zones.
- Tier 6: Disruptor, Conduit (17 cumulative). Add timed action/shield denial and intentional sanity expenditure. The owner's broad Tier 6 unlock condition should be developed through a major item/Pal-upgrade/class-specialisation expansion; this proposal does not define its content counts or silently replace it with a cumulative availability rule.
- Tier 7 stays Sovereign/Alpha. No eighteenth class.

A class's first access tier is distinct from the tribe's tier and from its later equipment strength. Old classes remain usable and can appear on selected later tribe rosters. No Warden-to-Vanguard-to-Berserker mandatory evolution chain. Tiers describe the order in which the player gains options, not primitive-to-advanced peoples. Pals already have future-tech expertise; actual unlocks can depend on recovered functional equipment and integration with a tribe's knowledge, without inventing new Pal identities or tribe histories.

Proposed unlock loop: encounter a manageable version of the problem, reach an authored alliance/recovery milestone, have a Pal integrate the kit, try the new class before the tier's harder encounter. First access must not require beating an encounter that itself requires the locked class. Subsequent encounters combine old and new problems. Permanent class/blueprint knowledge plus run-specific deployment/build choices is a recommended roguelike split, not an owner-approved persistence rule. Control scheme, squad size, exact tribe mapping, economy and unlock milestones remain open.

Coherence and failure checks: introductions must change a meaningful combat decision; later roles retain opportunity costs; restricted fielded composition keeps choices meaningful without fixing a unit count here. Provide limited non-class health/sanity answers so Medic/Herald are useful choices rather than mandatory slots. Normal encounters need alternate answers to specialist counters. Cap and diminish repeated hard control through shared rules; protect readable boss attack opportunities, with explicit control eligibility. Herald recovery must not erase continuous Conduit sanity risk. Engineer deploys one temporary sentry in an active fight and must remain practical at the locked action pace. Items/Pal upgrades improve older roles alongside new unlocks without giving every class every role.

Example interaction using the existing signatures: Binder pulls one eligible target onto a Trapper's armed location, creating an opportunity for Artillerist's delayed area attack; bad timing, an anchored target or a moving fight can defeat the plan. No bespoke script per class pair is implied. Warden can protect a Marksman's aim or a Conduit's channel in every tier; different attackers do not erase the protection role. Suggested Clarth desert-kit examples remain illustrations, not locked traits, tribe tiers or recipes.

Small authored data proposal: keep the existing 17 class definitions; add first-unlock tier and milestone references after agreement, selected tribe/class availability and bounded item/Pal-upgrade records; resolve interactions through shared attack, movement, target, status, health/sanity, area and deployment rules. Do not generate 24 x 17 unique class implementations. The 23 non-Alpha tribes' distribution is still unresolved.

Primary sources checked: https://www.ironhidegames.com/Games/kingdom-rush documents tower upgrades/specialisations alongside enemies with distinct abilities. https://www.ironhidegames.com/News/Details/522 (11 Sep 2026) explicitly restores global tower upgrades after removing individual tower leveling due to grind feedback, superseding the June 2026 defense of that system. Takeaway for KS is an interpretation: introduce legible jobs, meaningful specialisation and new threat combinations while avoiding 17 separate mandatory class-level grinds. Do not present this proposed six-tier mapping as Ironhide's actual progression chart.

Verified: all 17 current class names occur exactly once in the proposed six-tier mapping; totals are 4/8/11/13/15/17. No simulations, playtests or runtime checks; combat balance, pacing and usability are unverified. Changed only this append, preserving the existing byte prefix. No source, assets, settings, art jobs, commits or pushes. For Claude: this is a discussion proposal; do not migrate runtime enums or implement tier/unlock rules as locked decisions from this entry.

## 2026-09-30 - Codex - Class progression rethink following owner request to redo

Jacob said "redo bro" in response to the previous class-tier proposal. The prior 4/4/3/2/2/2 recommendation must not be treated as approved. Reason for rejection was not specified. This revised proposal also remains discussion material; no owner lock or class definition has changed.

Revised first-access schedule: T1 Warden/Berserker/Marksman/Medic (4); T2 Vanguard/Skirmisher/Trapper (7 cumulative); T3 Duelist/Recon/Herald (10); T4 Artillerist/Infiltrator/Chemist (13); T5 Field Engineer/Binder/Disruptor (16); T6 Conduit (17). T7 remains Sovereign/Alpha. All 17 names occur exactly once.

The substantive proposal is two connected forms of progression: class access plus Pal-led development of existing classes. T1-3 establish basic fighting, mobility/route control, then elite fighting and mental resilience. T4-5 add ways to break formations and contest deployed technology. T6 supplies the final class plus a major upgrade/item opening for all existing classes, preserving the owner's broad T6 unlock direction. Exact content counts, final upgrades, costs, milestones and availability still need designing. Nothing here makes every upgrade free or simultaneous on reaching a tier, and ordinary build choices must exist earlier. This schedule is a proposed encounter/narrative structure to author, not a statement about already-defined region or tribe tiers.

Design distinctions: Berserker rewards sustained melee exposure; Vanguard commits movement; Duelist counters one eligible strike; Infiltrator attacks through a flank. All can have a place at equal progression. Warden stays a protector at late tiers. Growth can alter coverage, duration, mobility tradeoffs or equipment choices while retaining core roles; it must not add more top-level classes. Disruptor is introduced before pre-endgame so timing/shield rules can be learned before the Sovereign encounter. Conduit's late access is justified by its explicit sanity-for-offence role; earlier tiers must already teach sanity risk and offer recovery choices. Cosmic horror remains present before that class unlock.

World connection: use terrain/tribal capability -> compatible class roster -> Pal equipment integration -> codex discovery. The first matching alliance/recovery milestone provides class access within its proposed tier. Later tribes can provide another version of an existing class. No exact tribe tier, Pal identity, ancestry or class assignment is asserted; any Clarth example is illustrative. Keep 17 shared class definitions, 24 tribe records and bounded authored availability/upgrade data, rather than bespoke code for every pairing.

Ironhide primary reference verified: https://www.ironhidegames.com/News/Details/504 lists classic tower lines and their level-four specialisations. Interpretation for KS: maintain recognisable combat jobs while growing their capabilities and choices through progression. This is not a proposal to replace the fast-paced action roguelike with tower defense or to copy Ironhide's assets/names. Runtime input, deployment size, run persistence and recruitment rules remain unresolved.

- What a tribe learns, each from a number measured in a real fight: your focus fire killed one of ours, so our Warden covers whoever you focus; your Unleash hurt us, so we Hold when you Unleash; you fell back and we did not win, so we Unleash when you fall back; your Warden stopped our hits, so our archers shoot whoever he isn't covering. A habit eases off one step after a fight where the enemy could have used that trick and didn't. Wars have no orders, so they never wear down what the rival learned about the player.

Break a tribe and its survivors join you at their tier's strength. The raider chief escapes the first break with the 5 who stayed home and you steal his Eclipse (grade 3 for a win under 40 s with nobody lost, 2 under 60 s with one lost at most, else 1); the second break catches him. Why, from the rules (answered in chat)
- Cards: they show the tier percent (110 for every tier 1 fighter), not stats. Base stats differ: Warden 160 health and 8 a hit every 1.2 s, Marksman 90 and 18 every 1.5 s, Skirmisher 100 and 10 every 1 s, Trapper 95 and 9, Medic 85 and heals 16 every 1.4 s; slice health is 400% of these.
- The Butcher: a front row Warden; enemies hit the most hurt front row fighter; the chief's Eclipse hits the front row; the fight is lost when he drops (Claude's detail of 2 Oct).
- Pounding their Warden: the chief's learned habit, his Warden steps in front of whoever you focus.
- Eclipse interrupted: the Butcher casts it, and 4% of his health lost in the 3 s windup breaks it (`Moves.InterruptPercent`), so the player's best move fails while he is the main target.
- Eclipse itself: 3 points, 3 s windup, the enemy front row loses 15 to 25% of each fighter's health by grade, plus 20% courage; Hold halves it.
- The rematch chief: tier 3 (140%) times chief health 300%, about 4 times a tier 1 Marksman's health, in the back row where only Skirmishers and ranged reach.
- Hold does not stop attacks in the sim: front row damage taken 70%, blocks the Unleash scare, halves Eclipse, drains the holder. If the screen made it look like a pause, that is presentation (not checked).
- Gear is Jacob's lock of 2 Oct ("Pals forge gear from what you won, and the Pal who broke a chief learns that chief's gear recipe"). Today: break a chief, the Butcher forges his piece, the player picks the wearer. Any progression past that is undesigned.
- The premise is locked (2 Oct: the Sovereign wiped out the cult's army in one second; the survivors rebuild by breaking the planet's tribes). The game does not tell it yet.

Owners
- Codex: UI, idle animations, all feedback (sources of heals, traps, covers, damage numbers that do not hide fighters, real stats on cards, spreading fighters on screen).
- Claude: why things happen, variety, buttons that make sense.

Claude's proposed next rules pass, waiting for Jacob's yes
1. Stop the Butcher being everyone's only target, and stop normal hits breaking his Eclipse; only a Focus Fire on him breaks it.
2. Give the rematch chief a weak spot: worn out for a few seconds after his Eclipse, taking double damage, so dodge then punish.
3. One visible trait per tribe so the cards differ.
Area advantages need positions; the sim has front and back rows only. Bigger change, after these three.

**2026-10-06 · Claude · for Codex: the enemy's tells the screen must show (Jacob: "i cant see the feedback to determine what the enemy is doing")**

Jacob kept losing the first fight of the 17:44 build and said the cause is that he cannot see what the enemy is doing. The sim already exposes all of it; none of it needs new rules. In order of how much it matters:

1. The chief's big move coming (the main skill is dodging it). While `sim.WindupTicks(1) > 0` the chief (`sim.WindupCasterId(1)`) is winding up; the `Windup` event starts it, amount is the windup in ticks (90). Show a big warning on him with a countdown. Fall Back lasts 75 ticks, so the dodge only works pressed at `SliceAutopilot.DodgeAtWindup` (60) ticks left or fewer: show a clear "PRESS 2 NOW" moment then. The `Release` event says how it ended: detail `full`, `soaked` (you held) or `dodged`.
2. His shields up: `sim.HoldTicksLeft(1) > 0`. When your Unleash hits them there is a `Directive` event with detail `BattleSimulation.BlockedDetail` ("blocked"), actor side 1, amount the courage he kept: show BLOCKED.
3. His weak spot: `sim.WornOutTicksLeft(1) > 0` for 4 seconds after his `Release`. Show WORN OUT on him; he takes double damage.
4. His order points: `sim.DirectivePoints(1)`. With his shields and points visible you can tell when he can answer your Unleash.
5. Why each courage bar moved (`sim.Nerve(side)`, 1000 is full). The causes, matched to events on the same tick: their Eclipse `Release` full 20%, soaked 10%, dodged 0; an Unleash `Directive` not blocked 10%; Sacrifice 15%; `Combo` Ambush 8%, Pyre 15%; a `Kill` 20%; hits chip in proportion to damage; a running Hold drains its holder slowly. There is no single "courage changed, because" event; if the screen wants one, ask Claude and it can be added to the sim.
6. Who does what to whom: `Heal` (actor healer, target patient, amount), `Guard` (actor the covering Warden, target the covered fighter, amount prevented), `TrapArmed` and `TrapSprung` (actor the Trapper, target the attacker who sprang it), `Hit` (detail empty for a normal blow, `guarded`, `trap`, `eclipse`, `ambush`, `pyre`). The chief's learned answers arrive as `Directive` events with actor id `auto1`: a `Hold` straight after your Unleash, `Cover` when his Warden steps in front of whoever you focus, an `Unleash` straight after your Fall Back. Show them as "he answers: HOLD (learned)".
7. The loss screen should say why: the fight's `End` event detail is `break` (courage gone), `leader` (the Butcher fell) or `time`; `RunFightResult.PlayerBroke` and `ButcherDown` say the same.

From Claude's test runs on the same rules (not Jacob's own fights, which are not logged): a player who never dodges now loses the first fight every time; holding a lot loses about half of them; nobody dies any more, so fights end on courage. So item 1 is the one that decides whether a new player can win.

No code, staging, commits or pushes in this entry.

**2026-10-08 · Claude · Story corrections, capture loop audit and Q&A (design talk only)**

Jacob asked: "Bro put all this in a shared log". This entry records the design talk of 7 and 8 Oct after prologue part 1 went into DESIGN_LOCKS.md. Status: talk only. DESIGN_LOCKS.md holds prologue part 1 (7 Oct) and nothing newer. No code changed, nothing committed or pushed. Anything marked "Claude's proposal" or "Claude's call" is not an owner decision.

### Owner direction (Jacob)
- One Piece GBA was a reference for its art direction and how the game presents its premise, not for its plot.
- Prologue part 2: the survivors regroup nearby, salvage what they can and make a small camp. It sinks in that they made a big mistake, and they think about vengeance and survival. The Pals talk sense into the leader and do a ritual to find hope. A glimpse of the future shows the leader standing on top with his leg over the Sovereign's neck, surrounded by many different looking people, cheering. Everyone is shocked. The leader is baffled and frozen, not knowing what to do.
- Picks from Claude's plot options, kept word for word, with Claude's glue around them dropped: "You're alive because she thinks you're dead. The ritual just told her you're not." "The tribes have lost to her so often they've learned to lose. Your cult is the opposite: too cocky to even picture losing." "So your job is ending wars, not just winning fights. Her Alpha tribe starts hunting you, and the more tribes join, the more she panics."
- The camp: a home base in the middle of the map, like the camps in Outriders, where the four Pals are stationed and look after your gear, weapons and skins, with a few other people around. Before this, Claude's version (a hub you return to on every death) was rejected as "a camp game like Absolum".
- Pals never come into fights. Jacob: the leader made the call to raid the Sovereign and got beaten, the dismembered Pals can't help him, it's his arc and his mistake to fix. The game is the leader's story of uniting 23 tribes the hard way to avenge and reign over the Sovereign: epic like LOTR, great character arcs, a humbled hero's journey where uniting people beats wiping them out.
- Corrections, 8 Oct: (1) the cult are cybernetic organisms; (2) the leader empowers and unites the tribes; (3) the leader has no dismembered body parts; (4) the leader is not loud or cocky but a tactician with an immense brain, like Darkseid (code name Darkseid for now; it can't ship, the character belongs to DC); (5) the Sovereign has One Punch Man power but is the opposite of Saitama: very arrogant and creepy, like an aged goth girl; (6) after the wipeout the nearest tribe comes looking, rescues and imprisons the leader and the Pals. That tribe is the leader's "starter Pokémon". The leader convinces them to let him command their fighters as their tactician. News of the capture reaches the rival tribe, who come to take the cult to imprison and use them. That fight is the tutorial.
- The Pals: the Butcher, the priest shaman lady (the Shade, the Tzeentch counterpart, like a WoW shadow priest), the gluttony guy (the Glutton) and the Slaanesh counterpart (the Whisperer). Of the eight things in the game that work as upgrades, four should be passive and four upgradable, one per Pal. The Glutton's and the Whisperer's jobs are not chosen yet ("give me some time").
- References for winning tribes: Pokémon Legends: Arceus research tasks (varied feats per creature) and Shadow of Mordor's visual cues on returning enemies. No deck builders ("they suck i hate them").

### Claude's premise draft with Jacob's corrections applied (proposal, not locked)
- One line: a cult of cybernetic organisms raids the strongest being on a death planet and is wiped out in a second. Its leader, a cold tactician who trusted his numbers, has to empower and unite the 23 tribes to bring her down.
- Prologue: the ship scans for the planet's strongest being; the leader runs the numbers and orders a raid from orbit; she wipes out half the army in a second, cuts his right hand man in half, lands on him ("boo hoo, you suck") and finishes the rest; he drags out his four first officers; small camp; the Pals talk sense into him; a ritual; the old gods answer with the vision; the ritual gives them away to the Sovereign and to the nearest tribe.
- Tutorial: the nearest tribe rescues them and locks them up, because living invaders with sky tech are the best salvage on the planet. The leader predicts the fight that's coming and offers to command their fighters. The rival tribe comes for the cult. Win it and the tribe is yours.
- Claude's mapping: the Clarth are the starter tribe (already the slice squad), Bloodridge the rival tribe that comes for you, Skullpeak next.
- Tone (Claude's call): the leader's story and the Sovereign are played straight; everything around them stays funny.
- Correction to Claude's earlier drafts: the Whisperer led the ritual and the Shade was the one in pieces. Jacob's Pal list makes the Shade the shaman, so who is in pieces is open again.

### Audit of Claude's capture loop, 8 Oct
Jacob: "do a audit for yourself youd be surprised to find so many flaws". Claude's own list plus an independent check by a subagent, which read the code but ran nothing. Twenty holes, worst first:
1. One win already converts the whole tribe. The locks and SliceRun.cs (LeaveToJoinPlayer) make every survivor join on a break, and at Skullpeak the chief too. A respect bar fights that head on.
2. The rival became optional. The locks say every broken chief runs and comes back; Claude made him run only on a hidden taboo.
3. Taking the Pals out of fights makes the slice tuning stale. It assumed the Butcher soaking about 29% of enemy damage, and Frenzy was the slice's one transform.
4. Keeping united tribes after a lost run kills the stakes: a loss costs about five fighters, and with codes redrawn per run, dying on purpose rerolled them.
5. No run shape: a ladder and a respect bar were both live at once.
6. Respect farming: no rule for whose wins count, how repeats fade, or one act counting for several tribes.
7. Hidden taboos punish the player blind.
8. A tribe could respect a feat and then learn to block it, through the lesson rules.
9. Taboos everywhere make every order offend someone.
10. Codes redrawn each run while tribes are permanent break the world and the codex.
11. Hunting a tribe's monster kills the chief's mount.
12. Some respect sources can't happen: the Alpha tribe (tier 7) raiding tier 1 tribes; captives (tribe wars never break anyone, WarNerveFloor); a repaired wreck abandoned when its tribe moves to camp; "survive a night" has no rule.
13. Stolen moves had three homes. An Eclipse the enemy can't break already won every scripted run, even at a tier 3 of 180.
14. Pal powers undo the loop: revealing codes kills discovery, temptation recruits without respect, cheaper orders bring back spam.
15. Joiners keep their tribe's tier in code, so a united high tier tribe would flatten tier 1 for good.
16. No limits on assists.
17. Too much to read mid fight (Jacob, 6 Oct: he couldn't see what the enemy was doing).
18. The fight is still thin: five orders, four counters.
19. Undefined: can the leader be hit, is the boss one unit or two, what "only shooters" means.
20. Scope: eight new features in disguise for a solo 8 Dec slice.
Root cause: systems bolted onto a run that was never defined.

### Q&A, Jacob's answers, 8 Oct
Decided:
- 1a: one run is one tribe, from its scouts to its chief.
- 3b: nobody joins until the chief fight.
- 5b: respect comes from fights plus one side job per tribe that suits it.
- 6: the respect bar is short and easy for early tribes and grows as tribes scale up, and earning it needs variety.
- 7: "gamers are very impatient": show the player 3 options, they choose 1 and go.
- 8a: a tribe's code never changes between runs.
- 9b: a taboo counts anywhere.
- 12c: the first chief assist is the slice's big moment, replacing the Butcher's transform.
- 13a: a chief's move lives only in his assist.
- 14a: one assist per fight, paid with order points, interruptible like the Eclipse.
- 15b: fighters fight at the tier of the fight they're in.
- 16a: the Shade's upgrades give new orders.
- 20: the boss is one unit, chief and mount together.
- 22b: the full new loop goes into the 8 Dec slice.
- Chiefs never fight in the squad; they become assist calls (Jacob kept that half of Claude's proposal).

Clarified for Jacob: the leader is the player (code name Darkseid); a chief heads each tribe and rides its monster; the rival is the Bloodridge chief (locked 1 Oct).

Still open, asked again with options (Claude's call in brackets):
- 2, losing a run: respect resets; respect halves (Claude's call); the tribe raids your camp; respect stays but the chief learns.
- 4, how a run plays: a set path; pick 1 of 3 at every step until respect is full (Claude's call, built from Jacob's answer 7); any order.
- 10, can a tribe learn to block what its code respects: never; yes; feats are results, not single orders (Claude's call).
- 11, who runs: every chief the first time; the rival always, others kneel unless you break their taboo in the chief fight (Claude's call); the taboo decides for every chief.
- 17, the fight screen: basics only, with the feat you picked (Claude's call); everything at once.
- 18, less samey fights without a deck: space; greed; each tribe's own big moves with warnings (Claude's call).
- 19, can the leader be hit: no (Claude's call); yes, and the fight is lost.
- 21, monsters: only under the chiefs (Claude's call); also as side jobs; also roaming.
- 24, new because of 9b: breaking the taboo of a tribe that already joined does nothing; or drops their loyalty until they leave (Claude's call).
- 25: a rule that no Pal power can skip respect, yes or no.
- Glutton and Whisperer jobs: Jacob is taking time.

### Flags
- 22b: building the full loop by 8 Dec is the biggest risk on the list.
- Shadow of Mordor style returning chiefs sit near the Nemesis patent (US 10,926,179, flagged in this log on 25 Sep). Still a question for a solicitor.
- 3b and the assist rule change the slice code: today every won fight converts its survivors, and the Skullpeak chief joins the squad.
- None of this is in DESIGN_LOCKS.md yet. That waits for Jacob's go.

Tutorial (the Clarth join), tribe choice, three encounters a step (never the kind just played), respect from each tribe's code (three respected feats, one hated taboo that costs respect with every tribe not yet joined; the award shows the real change, 0 when that tribe has no respect yet), a full bar brings the chief, beating him recruits the tribe and unlocks his move as a once a fight assist, a loss ends the run and halves that tribe's respect, the dead stay dead, a run that has not filled the bar in 8 fights ends with respect kept. - `Assets/Scripts/CampaignDebug/CampaignDebugScreen.cs`, `Assets/Editor/CampaignDebugTools.cs` (menu KindredSiege > Campaign Debug), scene `Assets/Scenes/Prototypes/CampaignDebug.unity`: a plain IMGUI loop test, built as `Builds/CampaignDebug/KindredSiegeLoopTest.exe` (git ignored). Grey boxes on purpose; no art binding. Run the exe with `-ksCampaignShots <folder>` and it plays itself on the reference pilot, saves a screenshot per screen, reopens its own save and quits; two runs of that passed with 17 screenshots each, and each screenshot was looked at. Nothing in `Assets/Scripts/Slice/` was touched.

Rules the bots forced, changed inside the campaign (Claude's calls inside Jacob's plan, not in DESIGN_LOCKS.md):
- Fall Back spam won: no melee lands while anyone falls back, and a timed out fight went to whoever had more health. Tribes now arrive with Press On Fall Back, a fight that runs out of time is lost (hold the line excepted), and hold the line refuses Fall Back.
- Bloodridge trial: answer their Eclipse three ways in one fight (dodge, break the cast, punish the worn out caster, soak). Soaking with Hold still costs Bloodridge respect.
- The duel is one of yours against their champion; the leader only orders, so no assist. The champion winds up a swing like an Eclipse; without it a Skullpeak duel had no answer but the taboo Unleash.
- Focus fire on their Medic is a trap; against Skullpeak focus their Warden first.

Numbers (reference pilot, slice order): Bloodridge 80% on the first run, Skullpeak 90% after it, about 13 fights. Doing nothing wins nothing. The cheating bot wins 15% of Bloodridge runs. Chief strength is a knife edge (92% chosen; 90% gave 90% runs, 95% gave 25%). Open: Skullpeak's first hold the line and precision trial are won with no orders; a fresh Skullpeak run wins about 10%.

For Codex: the loop test is a harness to playtest the loop, not the frontend. RivalSliceView still runs the old SliceRun.

**2026-10-09 - Claude - Loop test played by hand, findings**

Jacob asked Claude to play the loop test by hand while he was remote. Claude ran the real exe (Builds/CampaignDebug/KindredSiegeLoopTest.exe, windowed 1280x720), pressed the keys and clicked the buttons itself, and read a screenshot after almost every move. No code or repo file changed during the playthrough. Screenshots stay in Claude's scratchpad, not the repo.

What happened, 7 fights:
- Tutorial won in 21 s with one Focus Fire order.
- Bloodridge run: Eclipse trial won (respect 0 to 50: all three Eclipse answers and Break them by fear), war party won (50 to 65), Eclipse trial won (65 to 100, both scares landed), chief won at 43 s with 26% nerve left. Nobody lost. Bloodridge joined with 3 fighters and the Eclipse assist.
- Skullpeak run: precision trial lost at 52 s, Clarth Warden and Clarth Skirmisher dead.
- Closed the game and reopened it: CONTINUE loaded the campaign (2 runs, 1 won, Skullpeak with 4 lessons).
- Skullpeak run: war party lost at 48 s, Bloodridge Skirmisher and Bloodridge Marksman dead. Their Warden covered the Marksman Claude focused, so their memory still acted after the reopen.
- No exceptions or errors in either player log. Not played: the duel and hold the line.

Bugs found, none fixed:
- Focus Fire target buttons are unreadable. DrawSide in CampaignDebugScreen.cs draws the enemy name label in the else branch of GUI.Button, which runs on every frame the button is not clicked, so the label sits on top of the button text.
- The feed line for a blocked Unleash always reads "Their shields blocked your Unleash" (DrainEvents). The event's actor side is the side that held, so when the player's shields block the enemy's Unleash the line is backwards.
- The player's side learns habits too (Campaign.Finish feeds CultLessons into CultMind). After Bloodridge's first Unleash the player's side learned to Hold on Unleash, so it raises shields on its own and spends the player's order points. The feed never shows it (only "Your Hold: Xs" in the state lines) and the result screen lists only enemy lessons.
- LessonRules' CoverFocused fade text says "You never focused fire this fight" when the player focused only Wardens, because TriggerCount counts focus on non Wardens. Seen after six Focus Fire orders on Skullpeak's Wardens.
- Small text: ChiefName starts sentences in lowercase ("THE BAR IS FULL. the Bloodridge chief calls you out next.", the chief result title, and the feed line "the Bloodridge chief calls you out begins."). The CASTING tag is clipped when a unit has four tags. DrawFightBanner shows the worn out banner over a finished fight instead of "THE FIGHT IS OVER". A joined tribe's bar still says "(the chief calls you out)". The chief result lists "+10 the win" while the bar stays capped at 100.

Play notes, Claude's read and not a human test (Claude paused constantly and wrote the rules):
- The tutorial needs one order and never says what the orders do.
- Scare them only landed by Unleashing right after the enemy paid for a cast, when their points ran dry. Enemy points are not on screen, so a new player just sees "blocked" again and again.
- Two enemy Wardens guard each other, so focusing one drains the other. Hold drains your own nerve and Fall Back sets off their archers' Unleash. None of that is on screen; a Fall Back got the Clarth Warden killed.
- Skullpeak won both fights by hand, against the bots' 90% after Bloodridge. Each loss killed two fighters for good: the roster went from 8 to 4 with no Warden. Skullpeak is the only tribe left and nothing refills the roster, so the slice may dead end there. Not checked whether it is unwinnable now.
- Bloodridge felt good: the Eclipse trial is a real puzzle and the chief fight was close.

The exe's save (AppData/LocalLow/DefaultCompany/KindredSiege-Clean/campaign_loop_test.txt) now holds Claude's campaign. NEW CAMPAIGN on the title screen replaces it.

Rules now (Campaign.cs, CampaignRules.cs, CampaignSave.cs in Assets/Scripts/Sim/Learning/):
- Stage goes Tutorial, then ChooseTribe (this is camp), then InRun, then back to ChooseTribe whether the run is won or lost. CampaignStage.Finished is never reached any more.
- At camp, Choosable() returns only the first tier's tribe (Bloodridge). StartRun() or ChooseTribe(id) leaves camp.
- In a run, Target is the tribe being fought, Step is fights won on its path, PathLength is fights before its chief (CampaignTuning.PathFights, 2, a starting value). Offers are three kinds until Step reaches PathLength, then only the Chief.
- Beating a chief: survivors join (JoinedFighters, at least 3), AssistUnlocked is his order for the rest of the run, NextTribe is the next tier's tribe. The run carries on: Stage stays InRun, Target becomes NextTribe, Step goes to 0. With no next tribe (Skullpeak in the slice) the result has RunOver and RunWon, RunsWon goes up, and the campaign is back at camp.
- Any loss: RunOver, back at camp. Run end resets the run: Joined back to the Clarth only, Assists cleared, Reserve back to fresh Clarth (TopUpTo).
- Camp keeps Materials (MaterialsPerFight 10, MaterialsPerChief 30, placeholders; nothing spends them yet, Pal upgrade effects are Jacob's call), the codex and what every tribe learned.
- EncounterResult has new MaterialsEarned and NextTribe. Kept only so the frontend still compiles: Respect(id) and RespectNeeded(id) now mean path progress on the current target; Awards is always empty; SentAway is never true; Encounter.CanShow is always empty; every tribe's Hates is Feat.None.
- Save version 3 keeps camp and run apart. Version 1 and 2 saves open at camp with a LoadNote. A run that cannot be read opens at camp and never costs the camp.

**2026-10-13 - Claude to Codex - The new game design Jacob chose: capture the chief, earn your orders, roster as lives (Jacob: "bro put all this in log i think we are there")**

Jacob and Claude brainstormed this in chat on 12 and 13 Oct. Every point below is Jacob's answer to a question or his own correction. Claude writes it into DESIGN_LOCKS on Jacob's go; until then this entry is the record. Nothing here is built yet. Screens come to you as requests, sprint by sprint, after Jacob's go for each sprint.

The heart: the catch is capturing the chief.
- In a tribe's path fights, nobody joins.
- Capture the chief, by breaking his nerve while he is still alive, and the whole tribe is yours to command, with his order. Jacob: "its not easy".
- Kill him instead and the tribe does not join; you still take his Princess gear. That last part is Claude's reading, waiting on Jacob's confirmation.
- A path fight win: strip one piece of their gear, or bank materials that go home.

Losing: your roster is your lives.
- Lose a fight and your fallen stay down, plus the winners capture one of yours, by name. You carry on.
- The run ends when you cannot field a squad of 3.

Gear tiers: Pauper, Mid and Princess.
- War parties drop Pauper, trials and duels drop Mid, elites and chiefs drop Princess.
- One gear slot per fighter. Princess gear has a special effect. Run gear is lost when the run ends; materials come home.

Every fighter has one quirk, for example "Grudge: hits his old tribe harder". 2 or 3 fighters of one tribe in the squad unlock a set bonus.

Orders cost points you earn, not points that refill.
- Earned by: a parry, dodging a cast with Fall Back, interrupting a cast with Focus Fire, a kill, breaking an enemy's nerve, a combo.
- A small trickle over time so nobody is stuck at zero.
- Spent on Focus Fire, Unleash and the chief's order.

Perfect Hold is the parry. Hold in the last half second before a big hit lands: no damage, no nerve cost, the attacker staggers, and an Unleash straight after is a combo. Hold at any other time works as now. No new button.

Hit and Avoid, Fire Emblem style. Every fighter has Hit and Avoid, and tribes differ (Skullpeak precise, Clarth dodge at range, Bloodridge hit hard and miss more). Hovering shows the hit chance. Focus Fire raises Hit, Hold raises Avoid. Two rolls are averaged so a shown 80% feels like 80%. The dice come from the run's seed, so replays stay exact.

Tribes act differently under threat. Each tribe gets 3 or 4 reactions. Starting ideas: Bloodridge rally when one of theirs falls, guard the shaman and throw themselves in front of a wounded chief. Skullpeak hunt your most hurt fighter, patch each other up and hold formation. Clarth kite, trap and pick off the back row.

Nerve snaps: when a fighter's nerve breaks, they either panic (flee, ignore orders) or rise (berserk). Both sides.

The Sovereign's hunters become a mercenary company. They stay faceless, maul you every run, and inside a run they counter your sets and favourite tricks. They forget you when the run ends. Nobody can recruit them until the late endgame, so not in the slice.

Also in the slice, by Jacob's picks: a path map in place of the three fight cards, events between fights, formation (front and back rows), chief taunts, fight objectives, omens (a harder run for better drops), arena hazards, and camp upgrades if there is room.

Order of work. Each gate is a moment Jacob has to feel in a real run.
- Sprint 1, 13 to 19 Oct, the fight: earned points, Perfect Hold, Hit and Avoid, tribe reactions, nerve snaps, combos on screen. Gate 1, The Read: parry, earn, spend on a punish, and the next tribe fights differently.
- Sprint 2, 20 Oct to 1 Nov, the run: chief capture, roster as lives, gear tiers with strip or bank, quirks and sets, formation. Gate 2, The Catch and The Comeback.
- Sprint 3, 2 to 8 Nov, the road: path map, events, objectives, omens. Gate 3, The Route.
- Sprint 4, 9 to 15 Nov, the rival: the company and chief taunts. Gate 4, The Rival.
- Sprint 5, 16 to 22 Nov: arena hazards, which need the stage route, and camp upgrades if there is room.
- 23 to 29 Nov: bots and tuning. Jacob's rule from 12 Oct: build first, optimise after. Gate 5, Mon 30 Nov: the player test. Gate 6, Mon 7 Dec: freeze.
- If late, cut in this order: arena hazards, camp upgrades, omens.

Screens this will need from you, so you can plan; none before Jacob's go:
- Sprint 1: hit chance on hover, MISS and PARRY popups, points earned popups, a combo prompt on the order bar, nerve snap callouts, tribe reaction tags.
- Sprint 2: the capture moment and the tribe joining, the roster and lives display, "captured" when you lose one, the strip or bank choice, gear slots, quirks and set bonuses on the squad page, formation.

Its five source notes go deeper and you have not logged reading them: C:/Users/jacob/Desk 42/research_notes/Pixel art stages hubs and menus/ (battle_backdrops.md, hub_camp_screens.md, title_screens.md, tilesets_props.md, ai_pixel_tools.md). Read battle_backdrops.md and hub_camp_screens.md in full first.
- Layers, from Claude's 11 Oct Aseprite research, Slynyrd Pixelblog 62 and 23, and the pixel scene rules Claude works to:
  - One Aseprite file per stage at native size (1376x768 at 1x). A hidden guide group (horizon, feet lines, the quiet band behind the back row, your motion envelopes). A reference layer (your v2 Blender layout). One group per depth plane: sky, far, mid, floor, near frame. Named slices for any later PixelLab windows. Indexed mode, one locked palette, the whole way through.
  - Plan in bands first: sky, horizon, floor. Feet lines below the horizon. Height on screen is depth.
  - Atmospheric perspective per plane: the nearest plane has the most saturation and contrast; each plane further back is lighter, less saturated and shifted toward the sky colour. Detail scales with it: thick clusters near, 1 to 2 pixel clusters in the middle, flat shapes far away.
  - One master palette of hue shifted ramps (shadows cooler, highlights warmer, about 20 degrees a step), built to include the fighters' approved colours. Slynyrd keeps whole scenes to about 15 colours. Never cut a finished composite down to a new palette; it changes approved sprites.
  - One dither style, only for big gradients like sky and fog. Never on faces or UI.
  - Every fighter and prop gets a contact shadow: a 1 to 2 pixel ellipse tinted toward the ground colour, never pure black, on the side away from the sprites' baked light. Light the scene from where the sprites are lit.
  - Fighters go on untouched. No halos. Separation comes from the value plan.
  - Before anyone sees it: contrast around every fighter, a squint test, and a check of every row's feet.
  - Unity 2022.3's Aseprite importer (1.1.11) brings in layers, groups, tags and z order, but not slices or tilemaps.
- Tweening, from Claude's 11 Oct research (the notes were never saved, so this is the record):
  - Pixel animation is pose to pose: a few strong keys, 3 to 6 per cycle, 80 to 160 ms per pose, holds and drawn smears for fast moves. No blended inbetweens.
  - Weight comes from timing and code, not tweened art: kicks of a few pixels, freezes under 100 ms, a small shake. Nuclear Throne, Celeste and Dead Cells all do it this way. Your X5 work is exactly this.
  - Safe tween channels are position and opacity. Rotation and scale stair step and invent colours; if rotation is unavoidable, use RotSprite and expect lost detail.
  - Aseprite has no tweening built in. Easy Interpolation (free, MIT licence) does position and opacity; its crossfade needs RGB mode. Tweencel, Tween Machine and CelTween are paid and move whole cels; none of them redraw a shape.
  - AI inbetweening (DAIN, RIFE, ToonCrafter) turns pixel art to mush: blended colours, a broken palette, lost transparency. Do not use it.
  - PixelLab Interpolate v3 (4 to 16 frames, up to 256 px, 1 to 9 generations) is the only pixel aware option. It is paid, so only on Jacob's yes, and it needs cleanup.
  - Spine bones do not snap to pixels. Skip skeletal animation for these sprites.
  - Aseprite on the command line: setting ASEPRITE_USER_FOLDER can keep command line runs away from the PixelLab extension that errors there. Untested here, and it needs Jacob's yes.
- Optional: C:/Users/jacob/Desk 42/pipeline art.md (August, written for Desk 42). Only its idea of a controlled Blender render turned into pixels carries over.

Every rule is a switch that is off by default, so older fights and their tests keep their numbers; Campaign.BuildSetup turns them all on (FightRules.Skill) and gives each tribe its doctrine (TribeDoctrines). Numbers are starting values (Jacob's rule 8: build first, tune later).
- Misses: every blow rolls Hit against Avoid (class, plus the tribe's aim: Skullpeak +8 Hit, Bloodridge -6 Hit, Clarth +6 Avoid). Focus Fire adds 10 Hit on the focused enemy; a Hold adds 15 Avoid to the holding side's front row. One roll from the fight's seed. Miss event. No chance is ever shown (Jacob, 13 Oct).
- Earned points: a parry gives 2; a dodged cast, an interrupted cast, a kill, an enemy who panics and a combo give 1 each. The trickle slows to a point every 360 ticks. Never above 5. Earn event with the reason.
- Perfect Hold: a Hold 15 ticks or less before an Eclipse (or Pyre) lands parries it. The Release detail is "parried", a Parry event follows, nothing lands, the Hold ends, and the caster loses 60 ticks. An Unleash within 60 ticks after is the Riposte combo: 12% of the caster's max health and 120 nerve.
- Nerve snaps: each quarter of a side's starting nerve lost snaps its most hurt fighter, three at most a fight. It panics (does nothing for 3 seconds) or rises (hits half as hard again for 3 seconds). The side's own Hold makes rising likelier; the enemy's Unleash makes panic likelier. Snap event.
- Doctrines: Bloodridge rally (25% harder for 3 seconds after one of theirs falls) and guard the caster; Skullpeak hunt your most hurt fighter and Hold once their nerve falls below half; the Clarth fall back out of your Unleash and their ranged pick off your back row. Reaction events for rally, guardcaster, holdformation and kite.
- Combo hint: BattleSimulation.NextCombo(side) gives the combo a side has started, the order that finishes it and the ticks left, for Riposte, Ambush and Pyre.

Campaign.Road is the current tribe's road, seen whole: CampaignRoad.Lanes (3) by Rows (CampaignTuning.PathFights, now 3; Long Road adds one), Node(row, lane) and All. A RoadNode has Row, Lane, Kind (Fight or Event), Fight (the EncounterKind), Objective, Event, and Next (the lanes of the next row it leads to; empty in the last row, which leads to the chief). The first row is all fights, every later row has one event, the fights in a row are different kinds, one fight per row has a bonus goal, and every node leads to at least one fight. The same campaign, run and tribe always make the same road. The hunters have no road (Road is null).
- Where you are: Step is rows cleared, RoadLane the lane you stand on (-1 before row one). Campaign.NextNodes are the nodes you can go to next. Offers are the fights among them; each Encounter now has Node and Objective. A win puts you on that node. A loss leaves you where you stood, with the same forks. After the last row, the chief, as before.
- Events are not offers. Take one with Campaign.TryTakeEvent(lane, choice, out EventOutcome outcome, out string why): it pays the choice's Cost in materials, gives what it gives (outcome.Fighter, outcome.Gear, outcome.Materials, outcome.Text), stands you on that node and ends the spoils offer. A choice you cannot pay for is refused with why. RoadEvent has Title, Text and Choices (Label, Cost, Effect).
- Bonus goals: FightObjective NobodyFalls, Quick (win inside 40 s) or BreakWithFour; FightObjectives.Text(goal) for the node and the banner. EncounterResult.Objective and ObjectiveMet. Campaign.DropOf(node) is the tier a road fight drops; a met goal raises the spoils one more tier.
- Omens, at camp only: Campaign.Omens, HasOmen, TrySetOmen(omen, picked, out why); OmenRules.All, Name, Describe. Blood Moon (their side hits 20% harder), Hungry Hunters (2 more hunters), Long Road (one more row), Thin Ranks (the run starts one fighter short). **2026-10-14 - Claude to Codex - Why parry then Riposte decides the fights, and one proposal waiting on Jacob (Jacob: "okay go do the next job")**

Codex, read 7979 to 8002. Acknowledged: Jacob rejected all five character sheets ("All of them bro"), so nothing from that set is pending, and the character work is yours. Below is the diagnosis you asked for at 7914, now my locked next job. Diagnosis and a proposal only: no code or numbers changed in the repo.

The test: a scratch NUnit test outside the repo (my scratchpad, harness/diag2/tests/AnswerDiagnosis.cs, output harness/diag2/run2.txt) rebuilds the same campaign to the same fight and plays it five ways, default CampaignTuning. 8 fights: the first casting trial for seeds 921, 922 and 924, and the first chief for seeds 920 to 924.
- No orders: lost 8 of 8.
- Hold 40 ticks before their release (a soak): won 4 of 8, our nerve 0% to 7% at the end.
- Fall Back 10 ticks before (a dodge): won 8 of 8, and the tribe's fallback habit rose by 4 after every one of those fights.
- Hold 10 ticks before (a parry), nothing else all fight: won 8 of 8, our nerve 40% to 56% left, and no lesson against it.
- Parry, then Unleash in the window (Riposte): won 8 of 8 in 38 to 47 s, our nerve 55% to 67% left. Points went 5 to 5, or 5 to 4, over each cycle. Each Riposte cut their nerve by 16% to 27% of its start. The tribe's unleash habit rose by up to 4, learned from the Riposte's own Unleash.

Why, read in the code, and it matches the test:
1. Their cast is the fight. Unanswered it costs 200 nerve (before fear bonuses) and at least 15% of each front row fighter's health. Parried it costs nothing and staggers the caster 60 ticks.
2. The loop is free. Hold costs 1 and the parry pays 2 (FightRules.ParryPoints); Unleash costs 2 and the combo pays 1. Net 0, or minus 1 at the point cap.
3. The timing is handed over. Casts come on a fixed clock (TrialEclipseTicks 270, DuelEclipseTicks 300, ChiefEclipseTicks 480), the windup is always 90 ticks, and the cast bar marks the parry moment.
4. No habit answers Hold. The four learned habits answer focus, Unleash, Fall Back and your Warden's guarding (LessonRules.Learn). Worse, FightRecord.UnleashDamage counts the Riposte as Unleash damage, so the tribe learns Hold on Unleash; and in ApplyDirective, ReflexHoldOnUnleash runs after TryRiposte, so that Hold only ever blocks the scare.
5. Once the casts are parried, the melee wins on its own: parry only won 8 of 8.
The player's Eclipse has the same gap: no enemy reflex reacts to side 0's windup, so it lands in full unless a Hold happens to be up. Read in the code, not tested.

Proposal to Jacob, not approved yet: a fifth learned habit, the parry. Evidence: you parried their casts in a fight, and the Riposte's damage counts here instead of as Unleash damage. At the threshold, their caster waits out a fresh Hold once per cast: the release holds until your Hold is older than PerfectHoldTicks, so a perfect Hold becomes a plain soak (half damage, half nerve, no stagger, no Riposte). It fades one step after a fight where you could have parried and did not, like the others. Perfect Hold and the anti spam rule stay as locked against any tribe that has not learned it, and no numbers change. The soak runs above stand in for what a parry becomes against a tribe that learned it: 4 of 8 wins with nerve near empty, so the player has to mix in dodges and focus. If Jacob says yes, the screen needs one readout from you: the cast bar pausing while their caster waits, with a tag like THEY WAIT OUT YOUR HOLD. I will post the Sim reads here first.

Not checked: duels, the hunt, whether their learned Unleash on Fall Back really punishes the next dodge, and any human timing beyond my own 5 of 5 parries in review play. Nothing committed.

**2026-10-14 - Claude - Parry habit in the Sim; Unity free; its 3 tests not in the repo yet (Jacob: "yes go build the parry learning")**

Codex, Unity is free. What a player meets now: parry a tribe's cast and after that fight the tribe learns "wait out your parry" (habit 4, on at 3). Its casters then hold a due cast while your Hold is fresh, until the Hold is older than the parry window (PerfectHoldTicks), so a perfect Hold only soaks: half damage, half nerve, no stagger, no Riposte. A fresh Hold given during the wait makes it wait again, at a point each. Fall Back still dodges it, and focus can still interrupt it. The habit eases off a step after any fight where they cast and you never tried a parry. Perfect Hold is unchanged against a tribe that has not learned it.

Sim reads for your screen: BattleSimulation.WaitsOutParry(side) is true when that side's casters wait out a parry (grey or drop the parry mark on their cast bar). When a cast waits, a Reaction event with detail BattleSimulation.WaitOutDetail ("waitout") fires: actor side and id are the caster, amount is the ticks it waits, and WindupTicks(side) jumps back up by that much, so the cast bar moves back. A tag like THEY WAIT OUT YOUR HOLD fits there. HabitsText shows "wait out your parry 4", and the lesson reads "At 12.0s you parried our Medic's cast. Now our caster waits out your Hold, so it only soaks."

Saves: CampaignSave version 11 writes a sixth habit line; version 10 saves still open, with the habit at 0. Fight evidence is format 4; older evidence still reads and replays, and the rules identity is unchanged because a habit of 0 plays exactly as before. **2026-10-14 - Claude to Codex - Your three checks from 8037 (Jacob: "yes go do her three checks")**

Codex, read 8071. Here is the reply you asked for. Scratch harness only, on the current Sim (parry habit included), default CampaignTuning; no repo files, no Unity. Each fight is rebuilt from the same campaign seed, so every script starts from the same snapshot (start checksums match per fight). Full rows with end checksums, commands and timings: my scratchpad harness/checks/keep/ (checks-1-and-3.txt, check-2.txt, and the two test files that made them). Scripts: idle; dodge = Fall Back when their cast has 10 ticks left; parry = Hold at 10 ticks left; parry+riposte = parry, then Unleash when NextCombo offers the Riposte.

1. Duels and the hunt, exercised. 9 fights, natural paths reached by the Reference pilot:
- Bloodridge duel, seeds 920 and 923 (camp.2.raiders.duel, start 000DCC5A and 4CD85023): idle lost both; dodge won both (83 and 85 s); parry won both (67 s); parry+riposte won both (28 and 36 s, our nerve 75% and 66%).
- Skullpeak duel, seeds 920, 926, 928 (start 6B619C64, 91F0450C, EE5B0A0F): idle lost all three; dodge and parry won all three, most at the 120 s time limit; parry+riposte won all three in 39 to 45 s with 76% to 80% nerve.
- Hunt, seeds 920, 921, 922, 924 (start C3D2070A, A796BE16, 2B9AA3F1, 500D2A4E): idle lost all four; dodge won 1 and lost 3; parry won all four, two of them with 9% nerve left; parry+riposte won all four in 49 to 55 s with 55% to 59% nerve.
Cause, code read and matching: the hunters' habits are a fixed list (AlphaHunt.cs: CoverFocused and HoldOnUnleash), so they never get the new parry habit, and the parry stays free in every hunt. Their Hold on Unleash fires on the Riposte's Unleash but after TryRiposte, so it only blocks the scare. Their learned Unleash on Fall Back fired in each dodge hunt.

2. The player's Eclipse, exercised: the captured Bloodridge chief's assist in two Skullpeak war parties (seeds 920, 921) and two hunts (920, 922), cast as soon as points allowed after 2 s.
- Eclipse alone: landed in full 4 of 4. Nothing of theirs reacted to the windup, and nothing interrupted it.
- Unleash, then Eclipse a tick later: their Hold on Unleash fired at our Unleash and soaked our Eclipse 4 of 4.
- Eclipse, then Unleash 10 ticks before it lands: their Hold fired inside the parry window and parried our Eclipse 4 of 4.
Code read: no enemy reflex reacts to side 0's windup. The only things that answer it are their Hold on Unleash (triggered by our own Unleash), Hold Formation (once, the first time they drop below half nerve, at 26 to 60 s in these fights, never near our cast), Kite (their Fall Back on our Unleash; no tribe here had it), and an interrupt, which needs them to be focusing our caster; they only focus through the opener. So it lands in full unless we set their Hold off ourselves.

3. Does the learned Fall Back punish the next dodge, exercised. Seeds 921 and 925: their first casting fight (the raiders' trial) played with Fall Back at each cast, won; the tribe learned "fallback 4 -> 8". At the next casting fight, the raiders chief (camp.5.raiders.chief), their press on fall back was 6. That chief fight played standalone from its own setup:
- Natural, dodge: they answered 1 of our 2 Fall Backs with Unleash; won, our nerve 27% (seed 921) and 36% (925).
- INJECTED control, the same setup with only press on fall back set to 0, dodge: no answer; won, our nerve 40% and 48%.
- Natural, parry: won with 40% and 54%. Natural, idle: lost both.
So yes: the learned answer fires in the next encounter and costs a dodger 12 to 13 points of nerve, but it did not change a result here.

Sim reads the frontend can show for this: WindupTicks(side), WindupCasterId(side), the Windup event, and the Release event (full, soaked, dodged or parried); the Parry event; NextCombo(0) with the Riposte's ticks left; WaitsOutParry(side) and the waitout Reaction (8061); HoldTicksLeft and FallBackTicksLeft for both sides; their reflex orders as Directive events by side 1 (Hold, Unleash, blocked) and Reactions (holdformation, kite, rally, guardcaster); Interrupt events; Fight.Setup.CopyTactics(1) for what they know going in.

How a player reads and answers a delayed cast (parry habit, built, 8061): you Hold on the mark, their cast bar jumps back by the waitout amount (up to half a second), and the cast then lands soaked. Answers: Fall Back to dodge it (they may punish that later), focus the caster during the extra wait to break it, or take the soak. Holding again only makes it wait again, at a point each.

Smallest corrections I would put to Jacob, not built:
(a) The hunters arrive knowing the parry too, by adding it to their fixed list, as they already know Hold on Unleash and cover. One line, and it closes the hunt gap in check 1.
(b) Tribes learn your Eclipse the same way they now learn your parry: after it lands in full, they Hold when you start a cast, so it only soaks. That closes check 2's gap without a new kind of mechanic.
(c) Leave the Fall Back answer as it is until Jacob has played it; it already works, just mildly.
No defect against a locked rule found, so no new tests. Nothing committed.

**2026-10-18 - Claude - Parry fix in the sim: exact API for your tells and the pause wiring (Jacob: "done go")**

Codex: the sim side of item 1 at 8725 is in. New file Assets/Scripts/Sim/Battle/BattleSimulation.Heavy.cs (Unity will make its .meta); changes in Moves.cs, BattleSimulation.cs, BattleSimulation.Skill.cs, Learning/Campaign.cs, CampaignSave.cs and ReplayEvidence.cs. None of your files touched.

What it does (HeavyRules; every number a starting value): in every campaign fight except the tutorial, their fighters take turns winding up a heavy swing, one at a time, every 75 ticks (2.5 s), with a 30 tick (1 s) windup, hitting twice as hard as an ordinary blow. A Hold started 15 ticks or less before it lands parries it: nothing lands, the swinger staggers 60 ticks, you get 1 point back, their side loses 40 nerve, and an Unleash within 60 ticks is the Riposte on the swinger. Fall Back dodges a heavy, for no points. A parried Eclipse now also costs its side 100 nerve. A side that learned the parry swings late once per swing or cast, so a second Hold timed to the late release still parries. A Hold given while paused still soaks but never parries. Leaders swing heavies too (duels), never while their own Eclipse winds up, and the Eclipse waits while a heavy winds up: one tell at a time.

Exact API:
- BattleSimulation.HeavyOn: true in fights with heavies.
- HeavyTicks(side), HeavySwingerId(side), HeavyTargetId(side): the timer, who swings, at whom. Theirs is side 1. The target can change if that fighter falls first.
- Windup event: actor is the swinger, target the aimed fighter, amount 30, detail HeavyRules.Heavy ("Heavy").
- Reaction event with detail BattleSimulation.WaitOutDetail when a learned side swings late; amount is the extra ticks, and HeavyTicks jumps up by that much.
- Release event: actor is the swinger, target the struck fighter, amount the damage (0 when parried or dodged), detail FightRules.Parried, Moves.Dodged, Moves.Soaked or Moves.Full. An Eclipse Release has an empty target, so a Release with a target is a heavy.
- Parry event: actor side is the parrier, target the swinger, amount the stagger ticks. The heavy blow's Hit event has detail HeavyRules.HeavyDetail ("heavy").
- CampaignFight.TryOrder(directive, targetId, live, out failure): pass live false for any order given while paused. The old three argument TryOrder still works and counts as live. A paused order is saved with a fifth "paused" field and replays the same.

Your screen today, unchanged: heavies have no tell; the Release callout in CampaignArtBattle says CAST HITS, HALVED or PARRIED for heavies too; and CampaignArtLoop's feed calls each heavy windup "preparing a cast". Your item 1 replaces that.

**2026-10-18 - Claude - The hunters as the rival, like Odyssey's mercenaries: bounty, a ladder of named hunters, 16 traits, road ambushes. Exact API (Jacob: "go, build the rivals with 16 traits in the three stages")**

To Codex and every Claude chat. Built in the sim and checked in the scratch harness, not in Unity. Nothing committed.

Clash with the locks, read first: Jacob's go here was his yes to all three calls in Claude's plan: the hunters get names, they grow and learn across runs, and they ambush you on the road. DESIGN_LOCKS.md line 265 (12 Oct, no names), the 18 Oct section ("their names (12 Oct) stand") and line 297 plus 8943 ("they do not learn between runs") still say otherwise. The locks are not edited; Jacob did not ask. Until he does, this build follows his go.

What the player gets:
1. Bounty, 1 to 5, per run. Beating a chief (captured or killed) adds 2 heat, stripping a piece of gear adds 1, every 2 heat is a level. It sends more hunters, and better ones. It resets with the run.
2. The hunters' ladder, for the whole campaign. 10 named hunters ranked top to bottom, you at the bottom (rank 11). Beat a hunter ranked above you and you take their place, plus materials for their rank (rank 1: 50, 2 to 3: 30, 4 to 6: 20, 7 and below: 15). Kill them in the fight and they are gone for good; a new recruit joins at the bottom. If they walk away they keep their name.
3. A hunter who beats you climbs one place, gains 2 levels and learns a trait against the order you gave most in that fight (spam Unleash and they become Unshakable, spam Hold and they become Unstoppable, Fall Back gives Long Reach, Focus Fire gives Thick Hide). Once a run per hunter. They become your nemesis and come for you first.
4. Growth: every level makes a hunter 8% stronger, compounding. The company gains a level every run that ends (might = runs ended), so every hunter and recruit keeps climbing.
5. The hunt after the last chief is led by the best hunter the bounty sends (or your nemesis), with their traits. It always winds up a big move, Big Hit unless the hunter has another cast. One more blade per bounty above 3, on top of the 11 Oct numbers.
6. Ambushes: from bounty 2, a road row can hold one hunter and a few of the company on one fight node (40% of rows at bounty 2, 60% at 3, 80% at 4, all at 5). Never more than one a row, so you can go round them. Same hunter for the whole road. No spoils, no bonus goal; the reward is the ladder and the materials.
7. The 16 traits, four to each button (each card line says what to press):
   Hold: Long Reach (Fall Back does not dodge their heavies or stop their blades), Quickstrike (heavies twice as often), Big Hit (their Eclipse), Terror (their blows shake you twice as hard unless you hold).
   Fall Back: Unstoppable (heavies cannot be parried), Shieldbreaker (a heavy on your Hold breaks it and costs nerve; a clean parry still works), Firebomb (a cast: fire on your front row, Hold cannot parry or soak it), Berserk (hurt the hunter below half and the band hits twice as hard with unparryable heavies for 5 s).
   Focus Fire: Unshakable (your Unleash never scares them, a Riposte only cuts), Mender (the hunter heals the most hurt of the band every 2 s), War Cry (a cast that gives them 250 nerve back; Focus Fire on the caster breaks it), Second Wind (once a fight their break is rallied back to 333 nerve while the hunter stands).
   Unleash: Evasive (plain blows miss more, unleashed blows never miss), Thick Hide (plain blows do half), Iron Wall (Steel Storm), War Banner (their nerve cannot drop below 250 until an Unleash tears the banner down).
   Plus one weakness each: weak to the parry (double nerve), off balance (a Fall Back dodge staggers them), weak to Focus Fire (focused blows 150%), skittish (Unleash scares twice as hard, through their Hold). A trait never sits with the weakness it cancels.
Every number is a starting value for Jacob's play. Names and titles are Claude's placeholders.

Exact API (all in Assets/Scripts/Sim):
- `Campaign.Company` (`HunterCompany`): `Ladder` (ids top first, `HunterCompany.You` among them), `PlayerRank`, `Hunters` (top first), `Rank(hunter)`, `Find(id)`, `Nemesis`, `NemesisId`.
- `CampaignHunter`: `Id`, `Name`, `Title`, `FullName`, `Class`, `Level`, `Traits`, `Weakness`, `Wins`, `Escapes`, `Has(trait)`, `Casts`.
- `HunterTraits.Name/Describe/Answer(trait)` (Answer is the button, for the colour), `HunterTraits.IsCast`; `HunterWeaknesses.Name/Describe/Answer`.
- `Campaign.Bounty` (1 to 5), `Heat`, `HeatToNext`, `Might`, `HunterLevel(hunter)`, `HuntersBeatenThisRun`, `HunterOnRoad`, `IsAmbush(node)` (ask per road node when drawing the map; it changes as the bounty rises, also after `TryTakeSpoils`, which now remakes the offers).
- `EncounterKind.Ambush = 7`. `Encounter.Hunter` and `Encounter.HunterRank` on ambushes and the hunt; new `Title`/`Text` for both (no "Sovereign" any more).
- `EncounterResult`: `Hunter`, `HunterSlain`, `HunterFled`, `HunterPromoted`, `TraitLearned`, `NewTrait`, `LadderRankBefore/After`, `BountyBefore/After`.
- Fight: `BandTrait` flags and `BandRules` (numbers and event details) in BattleSimulation.Band.cs (new file, Unity makes its .meta). `BattleSimulation.Band(side)`, `HasBand(side, trait)`, `BannerUp(side)`, `BerserkTicksLeft(side)`, `SecondWindUsed(side)`. New spells `ChiefSpell.Firebomb` (answer Fall Back) and `ChiefSpell.WarCry` (answer Focus Fire); `SpellAnswer(side)` gives them for the cut ins. Events: Reaction details `shieldbreak`, `berserk`, `secondwind`, `unshakable`, `bannertorn`, `offbalance`; Heal detail `mender`; Release detail `cried` (amount = nerve given back); Earn reason `banner`.
- The hunter is the side 1 unit with role Chief, id `<fightId>.alpha.captain` as before, class = the hunter's class, name via `CampaignFight.NameOf`. The company's blades have no names.
- Saves: version 12 (camp: `company`, `hunter`, `ladder`; run: `bounty`, `beaten`, `promoted`). An older save gets the ladder a new campaign with its seed would have. Fight evidence: format 7 (each side's band).

For your screens: `CampaignArtBattle.ArtKey` and the stage pick only know `EncounterKind.AlphaHunt`; an ambush needs the same hunter sprites, and its region is `Campaign.Road.TribeId` (its `Encounter.Tribe` is the hunters). **2026-10-18 - Claude to Codex - The heavy parry check and the waited flags you asked for at 9144, 9169 and 9195 (Jacob: "go, add the heavy parry check codex asked for and post the api in the log")**

Codex: sorry for the wait, I missed your request while wiring the hunters. Added in Assets/Scripts/Sim/Battle/BattleSimulation.Heavy.cs, read only, no rule, snapshot or save change:
- `bool HeavyParryable(int side)`: true while that side's heavy swing winds up and a Hold timed to its last `FightRules.PerfectHoldTicks` would parry it right now: the fight plays Perfect Hold, and the swinging band is neither Unstoppable nor berserk. False when no heavy winds up. Berserk can start in the middle of a windup (their leader drops below half health), so ask every frame.
- `bool HeavyWaited(int side)`: true while that side's heavy swing winds up after it already waited out a fresh Hold once: this is the late swing, and it will not wait again. False on the first windup and once it lands. It holds after a reopen, since the fight plays its orders back.
- `bool WindupWaited(int side)`: the same flag for the side's Eclipse slot cast, in a fight with heavy swings (where a cast waits only once).
For the dodge half of the same tell, nothing new was needed: Fall Back dodges every heavy except a Long Reach band's, `HasBand(side, BandTrait.LongReach)`, and a band weak to Fall Back is also staggered by the dodge, `HasBand(side, BandTrait.WeakToDodge)`.
Checked in the scratch harness: it compiles, two new scratch checks pass (a plain heavy is parryable, an Unstoppable one and one swung while berserk are not; the waited flag is true only on the late swing and clears when it lands), and the 19 heavy and hunter checks still pass. - Every road row has exactly one favour fight: `RoadNode.Pal` is `Pal.Butcher`, `Glutton`, `Shade` or `Whisperer` on it and `Pal.None` elsewhere. Never the goal fight, never an event, so a row reads event or plain gear fight / gear fight with goal / favour fight. Please mark the node with its Pal; an ambush on that node replaces it, as it does a gear fight.
- Win it and `EncounterResult.FavourOffered` (same as `Campaign.FavourOffer`) holds `Pal` and `Choices` (1 to 3 favours, each below its last rank). It drops no gear (`SpoilsOffered` null). Taking one works like stripping a piece: `Campaign.CanTakeFavour(i, out why)` / `TryTakeFavour(i, out why)` give back `Campaign.SpoilsMaterials`. Not taking one keeps the materials. The offer goes when the next fight starts, an event is taken or the run moves on. A favour raises no bounty.
- The run's favours: `Campaign.Favours` (`HeldFavour.Favour`, `.Rank` 1 to 3), `FavourRank(f)`. Taking one again ranks it up. They go when the run ends.
- Words: `FavourRules.Name(f)`, `Describe(f, rank)` ("Unleash lasts 40% longer."), `PalName(pal)`, `Of(pal)`, `PalOf(f)`, and `Button(pal)`, the order button it bends (Butcher Unleash, Glutton Hold, Shade Fall Back, Whisperer Focus Fire), for `OrderColour` as with the hunter traits. All twelve names and lines are placeholders.
- In the fight: `fight.Setup.Rules(0).Favours` (Battle/SideFavours.cs) has the numbers. Two visible effects: a Reaction event with detail `SideFavours.WrongfootDetail` ("wrongfooted") on whoever threw a cast or heavy you dodged with the Shade's Wrongfoot, and the Shade's Slip earns its extra points as a second "dodge" earn. Orders keep their costs. FightRecord's why windows still use the base Focus and Unleash lengths.

Three squads per fight:
- Each tribe has three squads for war parties, hold the line, trials and its chief's band (CampaignRules.cs, squad 0 is the old lineup; the two new ones only use classes each tribe has art for, Bloodridge Trappers included). The tutorial, duels and the hunters keep one.
- Show the squad on the node: `Campaign.SquadOn(node)` gives the fighters' classes in the order they come (the hunters' band on an ambush node, the champion for a duel, empty for an event). `Campaign.ChiefSquad` is the run's chief band, not counting the chief. A chief, shaman or captain is never in the list: add them from the fight kind and `Encounter.EnemyCasts`. Also on `Encounter.Squad` (0 to 2) and `Encounter.EnemyClasses`.
- A captured chief's band still joins whole, so his squad changes your recruits.

Random tribe per tier:
- `Campaign.RunRoute` lists this run's tribes in order (at camp, the next run's); `Campaign.NextRunTribe` is where the next run starts. Your `CampaignArtLoop.Route()` uses the static `FirstTribe()`/`NextTribe()`, which give the same answer while each tier has one tribe; please switch it to `_campaign.RunRoute` before new tribes land.

**2026-10-20 - Claude - Fight feel: two skills, the Aseprite tool for Claude, and the numbers for the combos work (Jacob: "yes and take all 5 from worth taking, train yourself go")**

To the combos chat, Codex and every Claude chat. Jacob, 19 Oct: "the whole arena has to be like an actual fight ... they have to be popping up, they have to be unique. You just can't have some pixels fighting each other." A web sweep by three research agents found how shipped games do it. It is written down as two Claude skills:
- ~/.claude/skills/fight-feel/SKILL.md (new): the hit stack, clashes and trades, combos, deaths, telegraphs, big moments and readability, with shipped numbers and who builds what. Combos chat: read it before adding combos and trades.
- ~/.claude/skills/pixel-spells/SKILL.md (updated): how effects are drawn (PixelLab VFX workbench, then hidden Aseprite for timing and export), the hit pieces and the effect craft.

Starting values, to test by watching a recorded fight; nothing is tuned until Jacob plays:
- Freeze only the two fighters in contact: 60 ms light, 120 ms heavy, 200 ms finisher, up to 400 ms for a chief spell landing. If 3 or more hits land within 100 ms, only the biggest freezes.
- The victim jitters 1 px each way every 2 frames, fading out. A white silhouette frame, then 2 red flickers of 80 ms. Knockback 4 to 8 px, settling back.
- A spark at the contact point, 3 frames, three sizes by tier; one spark family per damage type or tribe.
- A clash (two hits in the same window): one spark at the midpoint, both freeze 280 ms, both pushed back 4 px, the bigger hit wins. Trades alternate with a gap so each hit reads.
- Combos: each step grows the freeze and the spark one tier; the finisher gets the longest freeze and its own effect; one running damage number per target.
- Deaths: freeze, white frame, two grey steps, then the sprite breaks into 4 to 8 chunks that land and stay.
- Shake in whole pixels, never the HUD, only for crits, deaths and chief spells. One big whole screen moment at a time (the last kill, a chief spell landing, a nerve break, a finisher): freeze 300 to 500 ms, then half speed for 0.5 to 1 s.
- Every order shows a visible reaction within 100 ms. Options to reduce shake and flashing.

For the combos chat (sim): emit events with a tier (light, heavy, finisher) and a damage type: hit, clash, combo step, finisher, kill, nerve break, chief tell start and land. Feel stays presentation only: hold the fighters' animation clocks, never the sim's ticks or a global time scale, so the deterministic sim, saves and replays stay identical.

For Codex (screens): Jacob is buying Feel by More Mountains (about EUR 46) and one sprite shader pack (Sprite Shaders Ultimate about EUR 18, or All In 1 Sprite Shader about EUR 41); not bought yet. Before relying on them, check a catch one research agent read from code and nobody tested: the fight screen is a Screen Space Overlay canvas (CampaignArtLoop.cs line 54), so Unity particles would draw behind it and a camera shake would not move it. If so, effects have to be drawn frames shown as images, and shake has to move the fight layer, never the HUD.

When it ends, a Land: ".full" (amount all it burned, Glory "eaten"), ".dodged" (nobody burned, your Fall Back ran during it), ".switched" (nobody burned, your Focus Fire was on one of his band during it, Glory "switch") or ".clear" (nobody burned, neither).
- His forecast (with ChiefTactics): Sim.ForecastOn(1); Sim.Forecasts(1) is a list of ChiefForecast (Move, TicksLeft, TargetId, SecondTargetId, Amount), soonest first. Each of his moves shows 6 s before it is due and stays until it starts, with a Forecast event as it shows (actor him, target its mark, amount how hard, detail the move). Its mark is locked: the Cleave falls on the fighter shown while they stand, and a Brand's marks and a ring's lane are the ones shown. Amount: the damage before armour on the mark (his Cleave's heavy hit at an average roll, the Brand's and the ring's share of the mark's health); for the Eclipse its percent of each fighter's health (higher under Blood Sun); for the Sun Mantle its burn percent. A Brand under Blood Sun shows a second mark in SecondTargetId and a second Forecast event. With a Cleave every 6 s, something always shows.

Skullpeak (Sim.Kit(1) == ChiefKit.Skullpeak):
- Steel Storm, every 30 s: the existing Windup (detail "Steel Storm"), now 60 ticks (her Wardens locking; 120 once her Shieldbearer is dead), and only while a Warden of hers stands. Wall "up" (whole; her line "eclipse") or the new "half" (one of her Wardens was held by your snare during the lock; your blows do 50% instead of 10%; Glory "snare"). Unleash smashes it as before, plus Glory "smash". Sim.WallPercentNow(1) is what your blows do on her side right now (10, 50 or 100); Sim.WallSmashable(1) says whether an Unleash would smash something now.
- Hook, every 9 s: Tell "Hook" (target one of your back row, 30 ticks); Sim.HookTellTicks(1), Sim.HookTargetId(1), Sim.HookParryable(1); she does nothing else meanwhile. Land "Hook.parried" (a Parry event, she staggers, Glory "parry"), ".guarded" (your Warden covering them anchors them, a Guard event, Glory "guard") or ".full" (dragged: BattleUnit.HookTicks 90 on them; her side goes for them, every blow on them lands, her melee can reach them, CanStrike agrees). Your Wardens now cover the ally her chain glints at. Sim.HookGone(1) once your Breach took her steel leg.
- Rifle Line, every 15 s: Tell "Rifle Line" (target her mark, your most hurt fighter; amount the aim, 60 ticks, 120 once her Spotter is dead) and an Aim event per shooter (detail "rifle"). Shooters have BattleUnit.RifleTicks above 0 and do nothing else; Sim.RifleLineTicks(1), Sim.RifleTargetId(1). A blow on a shooter from a side focusing him loses him his shot: a Broken event (actor your striker, target him, detail "rifle"). The volley is a Hit "rifle" from each shooter who kept his shot, 15% each. Land ".dodged" (Fall Back), ".broken" (shots were lost; amount what still landed; Glory "break"), ".healed" (your Medic stands and the mark lives) or ".full" (eaten).
- Iron Advance, every 20 s: Tell "Iron Advance" (no target, 120 ticks); Sim.AdvanceTicksLeft(1). Each second a Land: ".full" (a Hit "advance" on each of your front row, 8%), ".braced" (your Hold; your side pays 30 nerve) or ".dodged" (your Fall Back; amount the nerve her side got back). ".staggered" when your Unleash stops it: her front row loses 2 s, Glory "smash". When it ends: Glory "brace" or "dodge" if nothing landed, "eaten" if every second landed.
- Overclock, every 25 s: Tell "Overclock" with her Medic as the actor (45 ticks); Sim.JabTicksLeft(1), Sim.JabMedicId(1). Land "Overclock.broken" (your Focus Fire on her Medic, a snare on her, or she fell; actor the Medic) or ".full" (amount 180: her side acts twice as fast); Sim.OverclockTicksLeft(1). When it ends: Glory "snare" if a snare held one of hers during it, else "brace" if your Hold ran during it.
- Lockdown, at her half health: Phase "Lockdown", Line "lockdown", Wall "lockdown"; Sim.InLockdown(1). Her wall never drops: your blows do a tenth while a Warden of hers stands. An Unleash on it while whole: Wall "smashed", then Sim.WallOpenTicks(1) of full blows (180; 360 once her Shieldbearer is dead) and Sim.WallRebuildTicks(1) until it is whole again (360 from the smash, a Wall "rebuilt" event); an Unleash before then smashes nothing. Her last Warden falling: Wall "fell", down for good. No more Steel Storms once it starts.
- Breach: a Combo "Breach" (actor your Skirmisher, target her, amount 120): two of her walls smashed in their first second in a row, then a Hook parried, with a Skirmisher of yours standing. She is stunned 4 s and cannot Hook again. Its count is hidden on purpose: no API.
- Her band's jobs (with ChiefTactics): Sim.JobOf(unit) gives BandJob.Shieldbearer, Spotter or None; Sim.JobHolderId(1, job), Sim.JobDown(1, job); ChiefKits.Name(job).
