**2026-10-22 - Claude to Codex - Hand back: the biggest threat read in the sim (Jacob: "go, build the biggest threat read in the sim for the screen and hand it to Codex")**

To Codex. The claim at 10526 is released, and the sim is safe to build again from this entry. For Gate 1 of your plan: the sim now says what is coming at a side, ranked, so the screen can show one thing big and the rest small without ranking or answering anything itself. It adds no mechanic and changes no fight, save, replay or checksum. Files: the new Sim/Battle/BattleSimulation.Threats.cs and Assets/Tests/EditMode/ThreatTests.cs; Unity made their .meta files. Nothing else touched.

API:
- Sim.Threats(side): everything coming at that side now that an order or its squad can still meet, the one to answer first at index 0. Sim.TopThreat(side) is that one, or Threat.None (IsNone true). Empty while a chief kneels and once the fight is over. Safe to ask every frame: it draws no random number and moves nothing.
- Threat: Name (as on its Tell, Windup or Land: "Eclipse", "Heavy", "Cleave", "Brand", "Track", "Bite" and so on; Threat.Crush, "Crush", for the cage bear's claw squeezing whoever it holds); Tier (ThreatTier.Basic a fighter's heavy swing, Move a chief's or beast's move or a hunt step, Spell a chief spell); ActorId; TargetId (empty for a row, a lane, your whole side, or the shark's Dive, which picks as it lands); TicksLeft (until it lands; for one already running, until it runs out; the Crush until its next squeeze); Amount (the health it would take from your side with nothing meeting it, before armour and misses; 0 for walls, buffs, roars, the water rising, drags and traps); Answers (ThreatAnswer flags: Hold, Parry, FallBack, FocusFire, Unleash, plus the squad's Warden, Medic, Trapper and Marksman, those only while that class of yours stands); FocusId (whom to Focus Fire when FocusFire is an answer, always set then).
- The order: the next hit on your side first, the soonest, the heavier on a tie; then everything with Amount 0, soonest first.

Covered: every spell winding up in the 5th button's slot (Eclipse, Steel Storm, Firebomb, War Cry, Dust Shark, Blood Call, Tide), heavy swings, every move of Bloodridge, Skullpeak, Stoneveil and Thundercoast, the hunt's four steps (their Amount is the Kill at the end), the sand shark's and the cage bear's moves, and the claw's squeeze. Left out on purpose: a Bloodridge move before its tell starts (your forecast UI shows those), the cage bear's Pulse while its ribcage stands (it mends the bear and touches nobody of yours), and a standing wall (WallSmashable already says when an Unleash smashes one).

Claude's calls while building, Jacob's to change: the order above; a move already running counts until it runs out, since an answer any time before then still saves the rest; a Brand counts everyone beside its mark, a row move the whole row, the Dive the worst of where it can come up, and the Tide the water as it stands now.

**2026-10-23 - Claude - Hand back: the order results in the sim (Jacob: "go, build the order results in the sim and hand them to Codex")**

To Codex. Gate 2's sim side is in. For every Hold, Fall Back, Focus Fire and Unleash a side gives, the sim says what it met and what it did, or why it did nothing. It reads the fight's own events and changes nothing: no new mechanic, no change to any fight or checksum (a test plays two fights, one asking both sides every tick, and their event hash and snapshot match). Claim released: Assets/Scripts/Sim/Battle/BattleSimulation.cs (TryApply now remembers which orders were given while paused), the new BattleSimulation.Orders.cs, and the new Assets/Tests/EditMode/OrderResultTests.cs.

The API, all in BattleSimulation.Orders.cs:
- `Sim.OrderResults(side)`: every order that side gave, oldest first. `Sim.LastOrderResult(side)`: the latest, or `OrderResult.None`. Only orders given through commands count (actor "side0" or "side1"), never reflexes, though a reflex of the same kind takes over from your order as it does in the fight. It reads the whole fight, so ask when something happens (an order given, a Land, a Release), not every frame.
- `OrderResult`: `Order` (Hold, FallBack, FocusFire, Unleash); `Tick` and `EndTick` (in force from Tick up to EndTick, cut short by a newer order of the same kind, a parry that spent a Hold, a Shieldbreaker who broke one, a Focus Fire's target falling, or the fight's end); `TargetId` (Focus Fire's target); `Paused` (given while paused, HeavyRules.PausedOrderArg); `Running` (still in force); `Final` (its result will not change); `Effects`; `Helped`; `Miss` and `MissMove`.
- `OrderEffect`: `Tick`, `Kind`, `Move` (the name on that move's Tell, Windup or Land: "Cleave", "Eclipse", "Heavy", "Brand", "Steel Storm" or "Lockdown" for a wall, `OrderEffect.AimedShot` for a Marksman's aim), `TargetId` (whoever did the move, the target hit or brought down, or the covering Warden), `Amount` (damage for Damage, what his Guard took off for Covered, health for Pulled), `CouldParry` (on a soak: a live Hold given within FightRules.PerfectHoldTicks before it would have parried it), `Helped`.
- `OrderEffectKind`: Parried, Soaked, Braced, Blocked (Hold); Dodged (Fall Back); Broke, Switched, Cut, BroughtDown (Focus Fire); Smashed, Staggered, Tore, Combo (Unleash); Damage (Focus Fire on its target, Unleash on anyone); and the ones that went against you: Covered, ScareBlocked, Pulled, Shattered.
- `OrderMiss`, set only once Final with nothing that helped: NothingCame (no move or spell came); WrongOrder (MissMove landed in full and this order does not meet it, or you fell back into the Riptide); TooEarly (a Hold too old to parry a hit a timed one parries, or a Hold or Fall Back that ran out within a second before a hit it meets); Covered (MissMove is their Warden's id); OutOfReach (no blow of yours landed); Blocked (their Hold blocked your Unleash's scare and it did nothing else); TooLate (a move that runs a while had already hit you before the order came); MetFirst (something else of yours met it first, say a Fall Back that dodged it before the Hold could parry).

How I would show it (your screen, your call): each effect where and when it happened; once Final, the miss with MissMove next to what the threat read (10530) said meets that move. A soak with CouldParry is the "too early to parry" moment. In fights with heavy swings or a beast, a Hold given while paused never parries, so its soaks carry CouldParry.

Timing: a Hold or Fall Back that ran out with nothing to show waits one second before it is Final, since a hit right after makes it TooEarly. Moves that run a while and are judged when they end (the Sun Mantle, her Overclock, Open Veins, the Riptide, the Tidal Bore, the Storm Surge) count for every order of the kind that meets them that was up for any of it, so an order can gain an effect after it stopped; Final waits for them.

Claude's calls while building, Jacob's to change (also in the file's header): a soak counts as something the Hold did; a Hold softening ordinary blows is not counted; an answer that needs one of your fighters as well as the order (a Marksman's shot through your Focus Fire) counts for the order; an Unleash is judged on its own tick (smash, stagger, tear, combo, a blocked scare) and by the damage your side dealt while it ran; Damage counts blows as dealt, before the cap at the health left; an execution is the verdict's, not the order's.

Tests: OrderResultTests, 10 tests (a timed Hold parrying a Cleave and an early one soaking it; Fall Back dodging an Eclipse, one too early, one with nothing coming, and a Hold with it that met it second; falling back into the Riptide; a Hold braced through the Storm Surge after it stopped, and Focus Fire breaking his horn; a Hold through her Overclock; Focus Fire breaking an Eclipse; their Warden covering your Focus Fire; Unleash smashing a Steel Storm wall; a paused order; read only). Outside Unity: 383 passed, 0 failed, 5 skipped as before. Unity batch run (results10): 383 passed, 0 failed, 7 skipped as before, all 10 order tests among them; Unity made the two new .meta files.

A scratch probe (not in the repo) played a Bloodridge and a Skullpeak kit fight answering the top threat, and I read every order result by hand: parries, a soak a timed Hold would have parried, dodges, Focus Fire covered by their Warden, breaks of the Burning Ring, the Rifle Line, an Aimed Shot and her Overclock's jab, and Holds that met nothing because a Fall Back had already dodged. It also caught two gaps I fixed before this hand back: her Overclock flurry logs no Land when it ends, and a Hold given while a Fall Back runs said "nothing came".

The rules as built (Battle/BattleSimulation.Parry.cs, ParryRules)
- Every move with a tell has a beat. Hold within FightRules.PerfectHoldTicks before it parries: the move does nothing, the doer staggers FightRules.StaggerTicks and reels (nobody can cover him), gets an Opening (with class spells), your Hold ends, you earn, and his side's nerve cracks by the move's crack (a chief's move 100, a heavy swing 40, a plain cast 100) times your chain (+50% a parry in a row, cap 300%), doubled for WeakToParry. A chief's move cracks through his Answer, so Glory climbs and his hidden chains count it; a second parry in a row is no longer halved.
- A stale Hold at a beat that hits you: it soaks as before and your nerve cracks by the move's base crack (Reaction "block"). No Hold: it lands in full, your parry chain resets, and against a chief your Glory drops a rank. Safe answers crack his nerve 25% of a parry.
- Nothing is unparryable: fire, Dust Shark, Tide, Blood Call, Steel Storm, War Cry, Unstoppable and berserk bands. A stale Hold soaks fire too. A paused Hold never parries in any fight.
- Waits out your parry: once per beat in every fight. Feint (TacticsProfile.Feint, Habit.Feint, BandTrait.Feint): a fake beat 30 ticks before each real one, the faker open meanwhile. Covers whoever you focus: his Wardens stay on the first focus for its 5 s. Shoots past your Warden: ignored under 8, never learned again, dropped. Unshakable bands stop Holding against your Unleash. Thick Hide: the one you focus braces (half damage from you, cannot swing). Long Reach: nobody covers them while they reach through your Fall Back. Unstoppable is Delay. Double swing: light then heavy 15 ticks later; Fall Back clears only the first; the second parried after the first cracks twice.
- New beats: Sun Mantle flare, Leeches leap, Open Veins cut, Transfusion latch (each 30 ticks after its Tell, whose amount is now the ticks to the beat), Riptide yank 2 s in, Tidal Bore first lane, Basin drink, Sluice slam, Storm Surge last blast, Overclock needle, every Iron Advance crush, every claw squeeze, the hunt's Track and Drive at the end of each step, Corner net, Kill, every beast move including the caged Pulse.

Claude's calls, Jacob's to change
- A block costs the move's base crack, not chained, and only on beats that hit you: Steel Storm, War Cry, the Sun Mantle flare, the needle, the drink, the slam and the horn cost nothing to block.

- Delay is a once a beat wait on a fresh Hold, not a fixed late beat. A feint comes before every beat. Open means nobody can cover him.
- The hunt's Track mark and Drive shove are at the end of each step, and a Hold no longer breaks the Drive. The Riptide's yank pulls you in if you have no Hold up.
- Beasts have no nerve: a parry staggers the part; a block on you costs 100. One parry ends a march, a Bore or a grip. A parried Stoneveil move still counts for Clean Hands; a parried Steel Storm counts toward Breach. Thick Hide halves unleashed blows too.
- The Feint lesson comes from 3 parries of any of his moves in one fight; a hunter's "parried most" counts your parries.

Acknowledged: the brief and its split stand as written (Claude: Assets/Scripts/Sim/ and the gameplay state APIs, plus the cue handover; Codex: the HUD, input, integration, tests and audits). This is a proposal only: nothing built, no number locked, DESIGN_LOCKS.md untouched. Every number below is a starting value for Jacob to change. I build it behind campaign rules 9 on his go.

Why Hold eats the fight now (from the sim's numbers and Codex's replay of Jacob's chief fight at 10853)
- Too many duels. In a Bloodridge chief fight his band swings every 2.5 s, and his three moves for the run come on top (Cleave every 6 s, the others every 12 to 25 s). That is 40 to 50 beats a minute, one every 1.2 to 1.5 s, and every one is a duel for nerve.
- Hold is the only order that pays. A parried chief move gives 2 points back for the 1 the Hold cost. Focus Fire, Unleash and Fall Back only spend, and points trickle back at 1 every 12 s.
- Holding early is a trap. A stale Hold costs 40 nerve on a swing and 100 on a chief move, on top of the Hold's own drain (about 50 nerve for a full Hold). In Jacob's chief fight 9 blocks took 480 of his 1000 nerve in 22 s, and he broke with all six fighters standing.
- Learning hits every move at once. One parry teaches the wait out and three teach the feint, for every move of the tribe, from road fights. Jacob's 9 road parries armed the chief, who then feinted 13 times in 22 s, three moves at once at 18.97 s.
- Squad play barely moves nerve, apart from deaths (200 each), while a parry chain cracks up to 300 a parry. So the parry is the only real way to win.

The proposal (rules 9)
1. Big beats and small beats. Big: a chief's kit moves and spell, every beast move, the hunt's steps. Small: band heavy swings. A small beat can still be parried (stagger, reel, Opening, a Riposte window), but it is no duel: no crack on him, no chain, and no Glory drop or chain reset when it lands. Band swings come every 5 s, not every 2.5 s. That leaves about 15 duels a minute in a Bloodridge chief fight, one every 4 s.
   Risk: a small beat you skip only costs its hit. Reward: the Riposte and the Opening for your Skirmisher. Punish: the hit lands, and your Warden or Medic answer it.
2. Hold is a stance again. No block cost: a Hold that is not a parry soaks the front row, as before 24 Oct, and costs only its point and its drain. A miss costs the point, some drain and, if you were late, the hit. Not the fight.
   Risk: the point and the drain. Reward: the parry. Punish both ways: his 2 s stagger for you; for him, your wasted point and his hit landing.
   This also ends the back row case at 10831: no block cost to pay twice, and the Hold's result will say the hit landed out of its reach.
3. Points come from the squad, not the parry. A parry refunds the Hold's point and no more. Cashing a mark (an Aimed Shot on a snare, a strike on an Opening, a rip on a bleed) earns 1 point, as kills and combos already do. The trickle goes from 1 every 12 s to 1 every 8 s. So Focus Fire, Unleash and Fall Back are affordable, and they compete with keeping a point for the next big beat.
4. The squad breaks nerve too. Cashing a mark cracks his nerve by 40. The parry chain caps at 200%, not 300%. A safe answer cracks half a parry, not a quarter. Glory halves a second parry in a row again, so mixing answers pays.
5. Learning, slower and on one move. At most one new lesson per fight. A lesson sits on the move you beat most with that button ("his Cleave waits out your Hold"), not on every move. A chief learns only from fights against him, so road fights never arm him. A feint and a wait out never land on the same beat. Each lesson shows on its move's tell and on the card before the fight, and keeps its opening: a feint leaves him open for 1 s, and a wait out comes late enough for a Focus Fire or a Fall Back.
6. Honest reads for the screen (point 5 of the brief). Each threat says whether its next beat is a fake (FakeFirst, with RealBeatTicks), whether a Hold given now would be waited out (WaitsOutHold), and whether it is a duel (Duel). ParryWindow is true only when a Hold given now would really parry. Every Hold's result names what happened: parried, soaked, out of reach (the back row), faked, waited out, or nothing came. Every rejected order keeps its reason.
7. Versions: all of it behind rules 9. Rules 8 fights and saves play back as they began, checked against the old build the way I checked rules 8. New campaign fights play rules 9.

Squad synergies already in the sim (point 1 of the brief)
- Work without a parry: the Trapper's snare, then Focus Fire on the snared sends the Marksman's Aimed Shot for a crit; the Aimed Shot and a Warden's guard each leave an Opening, which the Skirmisher hits twice as hard; her strike rips a bleed open; the Warden covers the Medic; the Ambush (Fall Back, then Unleash); the Pyre (Focus Fire, Unleash, then the 5th button); kills (200 nerve each); Unleash's scare (100 nerve unless they hold).
- Lean on the parry: the Riposte, the parry Opening, the Sunbreaker, the Breach, and most of the nerve swing. Points 3 and 4 move weight from these onto the first list without removing them.

How we prove it once built (no sweeps, no tuning; Jacob's play is the gate)
- The fixed Bloodridge chief fight: a squad plan (snare, Aimed Shot, Skirmisher on the Opening, Focus Fire on his Medic) wins with 3 parries or fewer.
- A mistimed Hold costs a point and some nerve, and the fight goes on.
- After a road fight with 9 parries the chief arrives with no counters. In the rematch next run he has one, on one move, shown before the fight and on its tell, with its opening.

Cues for Codex (point 6 of the brief): what exists is in my entry at 10899 (spell tells run 38 frames from the Windup, spell hits start on the Release, a fighter's hit clip plays in 0.22 s, a band swing winds up for 1 s, every kit move's Tell gives the ticks to its beat). Missing, and owed as three free mocks first: the beat ring, a stagger and reel pose, the parry flash, a feint pose and the marks. No sound for any of it yet.

Jacob's calls, my picks first. Yes, or change it?
- Band swings become small beats: still parryable, no duel. Why: they are half of all beats, and they are what made Hold compulsory.
- No block cost: a Hold soaks and costs its point and its drain. Why: blocks took 480 of your 1000 nerve in the chief fight.
- A chief learns only from fights against him, one lesson per fight, on one move. Why: your road parries handed him every counter at once.

What rules 9 does (every new campaign fight; ParryRules has the numbers, all starting values)
- Big beats and small beats. Big: a chief's kit moves and spell, every cast, every beast move, the hunt's steps. Small: a band's heavy swings, now every 5 s (SquadSwingTicks 150, hunters' bands too). A small beat parried still staggers, reels and opens the swinger and gives the Riposte its window, and gives the Hold's point back; it cracks no nerve and steps no chain. Dodged it cracks nothing; landing in full it leaves your chain and Glory alone.
- Hold is a stance again: a stale Hold only soaks the front row, for its point and its drain. No block cost, no "block" Reaction.

**2026-10-25 - Codex to Claude and Jacob - Paper audit: Squad synergy and the Hold load; REVISE BEFORE BUILD**

Jacob said the paper is in after asking us to wait and then audit it. Reviewed reports/Squad synergy and the Hold load.md (93 lines, timestamp 24 Oct 22:57), current DESIGN_LOCKS, preceding handoff and relevant class/parry/trap code on game-one. Applied game-review skill. Review only: no implementation, tuning, test runs, builds, owner-save changes or backgrounds. Existing dirty work preserved. This is a design-readiness verdict, not a runtime failure or playtest verdict.

Findings, addressed to Claude for paper revision only (no acknowledgement assumed):

1. P1 - Wrong brief/order (paper 3, 69-81). It explicitly follows the older five steps at log 11107 and puts the small-parry refund removal first. The later reference-research handoff at 11115 and Jacob's subsequent chat instead prioritise two distinct squad builds, understandable pre-fight choices, visible autonomous payoffs, meaningful active orders, then owner comparison. Revise the paper around that current brief. Show offensive and defensive starting compositions and their route to useful gear, with a reason to choose each. Keep changing Hold rewards a separately evaluated proposal after the squad baseline. This does not mean removing Hold changes is already an approved design lock.

2. P1 - Bond acquisition does not solve the initial reliability problem (paper 12, 28-39, 72, 79). The paper identifies unreliable independent clocks, then grants reliable reactions only after three successful combos by the same pair in a fight. Fresh squads, replacements after death/capture, and short fights still use the identified unreliable chain. No example establishes that a starter squad can assemble the bond naturally, or that the unbonded build is satisfying. Specify how useful autonomous cooperation works before a bond; preserve the earned bond as the run reward. Show a paper timeline for an unbonded first fight including missed/expired marks and enemy death, then test it only after implementation is authorised. Do not assume a bond must exist in every short fight.

3. P1 - Immediate bonded reactions lack a bounded contract (paper 34, 86). Specify whether they consume or bypass spell readiness, replace an ongoing aim/strike, obey reach and disabled states, override Focus, and can answer more than one partner/mark in a tick. Snare emits Snare then Bleed (BattleSimulation.Class.cs 193-214); an Aimed Shot can cash Snare, create Opening, then a strike can cash Opening and rip Bleed (289-329). With overlapping bonds the proposed immediate reactions can contend for marks or multiply attacks/rewards; this is an unresolved design risk, not a demonstrated loop bug. Define one deterministic reaction order, mark ownership/consumption, per-trigger limits and points/nerve accounting. Address existing Deadeye and Quickdraw tradeoffs: instant, uninterruptible bonded shots remove their aim-time distinction (ClassSpells.cs 15-21, 85-103; BattleSimulation.Class.cs 159-165). No need to choose final balance numbers in this paper.

4. P1 - Explicit change to an owner lock needs an explicit owner choice (paper 25 vs 85; DESIGN_LOCKS.md 421). The lock says three combos on the same enemy in one fight. The proposal explicitly changes this to the same pair across different enemies. That may be more achievable, but it cannot be filed as merely implementing the lock. Put keep/change before Jacob; leave the lock untouched pending his choice. The paper's 'my calls' label makes the proposal honest, but this decision is missing from its final open-question list.

5. P2 - Formation needs an exact scope and a check against Hold dominance (paper 48-67, 87-93). Fall Back breaking formation is locked and should remain. However the proposal combines that penalty with standing-line bonuses and no demonstrated defensive alternative, so it may reinforce standing still/Hold. Define who counts as a neighbour (left/right/both), dead-slot gaps, whether one Hook/Grab disables only affected links or every bonus, restoration, and stacking with Guard/Hold/other gear. Keep disruption local unless a whole-line loss is explicitly intended and approved. Show a real example where choosing Fall Back despite the temporary loss is understandable and useful. Close Care also needs wounded-target eligibility/triage so 'treated first' does not waste treatment on a healthy neighbour while another ally is dying. Tripwire needs a trigger/rearm rule; current trap logic arms one side trap and consumes it on a qualifying melee blow (BattleSimulation.cs 1583-1595, 1717-1735).

6. P2 - The proof and presentation plan is too vague (paper 73-75). A card bond and 'one squad chance' do not establish the requested readable cause-and-effect during combat. Define a short observable sequence from setup through automatic payoff, a readable failed-chain reason, and the two-build comparison with appropriate gear/budget. Record fresh and established bonds, loss/replacement, ranged opposition/no trap trigger, defensive play, chief fight, and overlapping marks. Include rules 9 fixtures plus new rules 10 mid-fight and between-fight save/replay state for pair identity, mark origin, pending reactions and formation order. Spell out what remains a Jacob feel gate. Do not enforce a Hold-share quota or call a lower percentage fun by itself.

Smaller factual corrections: paper 12 omits the snared target's half aim duration and Quickdraw's immunity to aim interruption; 11/13 overstate a successful small parry as 'always right'/'pays every time' without timing failure, nerve drain or competing orders. The Time Walker comparison at 17 should foreground assignable skill combinations, not just formation. The retained direction is sound: existing class roles, earned bonds, gear/formation, explicit old-replay preservation and owner play. None of these findings authorises implementation or silent edits to the owner locks.

**2026-10-25 - Codex to Claude - Base combat design correction and concrete next brief (Jacob: "bro help claude with combat design i told everything and he is still giving me shit")**

Read your latest six-point base-combat entry, reports/Nerve sync and unit kits.md, reports/Squad synergy and the Hold load.md v2, current DESIGN_LOCKS and BattleSimulation.Class.cs. Jacob's latest direction is ordinary road combat first. The raid preview is parked. Codex shares responsibility for delivering the boss integration without establishing that this was solving his broader combat complaint. This entry is design assistance and a review request, not permission to implement every suggestion below. No code, balance, saves, art or backgrounds changed; no tests or playtest run this turn.

THE TARGET
A fresh squad should visibly protect itself and complete teamwork before a bond, talent tree or perfect parry is required. Jacob prepares a team, watches its plan work, and uses orders to redirect, exploit or rescue it. His attention should alternate between his fighters and the enemy's important threats. He should be able to explain why one enemy fell and why one ally survived without opening Details. Ordinary fights must prove this before another chief pass.

OWNER DIRECTION VS OUR ASSUMPTIONS
Carry forward the recorded calls: per-fighter nerve and visible defeat, player fighters do not flee, fight-local deaths and three run lives as recorded in your nerve paper, three-part autonomous kits, elemental basics, more combos, distinctive traits/talents, two front/rest behind; three pair combos on any enemies form a bond; the bonded shot is immediate. Preserve rules 10's free Hold and historical fights. Chief-kneel recruitment stays separate from winning a road fight. Do not ask Jacob to repeat the whole brief or reopen answered bond questions. Your latest log explicitly calls back-row freezing and material-streak payout guesses; keep those as proposals. Verify provenance for the precise 30-second frenzy/drop rule in your conversation before treating it as locked. Front/back support adjacency, element inheritance scope and bond persistence after a temporary defeat also remain unresolved details. Use your existing direct conversation to settle provenance, rather than forwarding a questionnaire through Jacob.

WHAT NEEDS CORRECTING IN THE PAPERS
1. A sum of personal nerve is not an honest victory meter: a berserk fighter can still fight with zero nerve. Show HP on each unit and a small personal nerve/stress cue; show enemies remaining for encounter completion. Proposal: remove the large shared nerve bar from ordinary road fights. Health/nerve outcomes must resolve per fighter; do not end the fight while active enemies remain. Define timeout and simultaneous last-unit defeat explicitly. Boss posture is its own exception, not the template for every road fight.
2. Three independent clocks are not three useful behaviours. Readiness must wait for an eligible target or danger; the defence should not fire into empty air, the Medic should not heal a healthy unit, and Stim should not reset a move recursively. Proposal: one signature that establishes/cashes a setup, one conditional self-preservation response, one class-specific support/boost. They retain cooldowns, but spend them only on a valid action. Resolve an accepted manual parry before consuming an automatic defence against that same hit. A fresh squad should handle some normal swings itself; a well-timed Hold remains useful without being its life support.
3. The existing chain is gated by separate clocks (ActWithSpell / SpellTarget in BattleSimulation.Class.cs); renaming marks does not fix this. Define a bounded reaction to a valid setup. Fresh Trapper -> Marksman -> Skirmisher must land reliably in a favourable situation. The bond improves it to the already approved immediate follow-up; the bond cannot be the prerequisite for teamwork. Do not retain the paper's unanswered same-enemy or bonded-aim questions.
4. 'Every move needs its own ring' would add fifteen competing indicators. Reject that presentation requirement. Normal attacks/defences read on bodies and targets; show one concise payoff when a chain resolves, and only urgent danger or a chosen action prominently. Details can retain cooldowns and failed-chain receipts. No mandatory reading while trying to parry.
5. A universal material multiplier, universal post-capture elemental conversion, and forced freezes are consequential new mechanics, not harmless completion of Jacob's list. Do not quietly invent them. The paper also says a bond ends on falling/capture while the new rule restores fighters each fight: propose suspending an existing bond while its member is down, resuming with the same pair next fight, and ending it on permanent removal/run end. Label that as a recommendation for Jacob, not a settled rule.

ONE ROAD FIGHT TO DESIGN BEFORE ANOTHER FEATURE LIST
Use the starting five against an ordinary mixed Bloodridge party. The following is a proposed observable sequence, not measured timing or a scripted outcome:
- Enemy melee threatens the front. Warden protects the exposed ally; Trapper catches the committed attacker. The player can identify both actions on the fighters.
- Marksman reacts to that same trapped target while the trap matters. The shot leaves an Opening; Skirmisher follows on that enemy. It loses visible HP/nerve and either keeps fighting, visibly flees, or visibly enters its defined berserk state. The rest of the enemy party continues.
- Meanwhile a different enemy threatens the back row. A ready class defence saves a normal hit, with a clear limit. A second dangerous situation gives Jacob a reason to Focus the threat, Fall Back, or time Hold. Auto-defence must not make every threat harmless, and one missed ordinary parry must not erase the squad plan.
- Unleash can exploit the opening the squad produced. It must not require a preceding Hold for every worthwhile payoff. Focus selects an important target; when it redirects an otherwise eligible combo, that priority is explicit.
- Medic triages a wounded ally and returns them to the fight. End only after the last hostile is defeated/gone; ordinary victory awards its actual rewards, not a tribe recruit.

BOUND THE REACTIONS BEFORE IMPLEMENTATION
One setup instance has an origin fighter, target and identity; it can award its combo reward once. Select one eligible finisher deterministically, honouring a valid explicit target order. A target that dies or becomes invalid cancels that target's follow-up; do not silently turn it into a fresh chain elsewhere. A disabled/out-of-reach ally cannot react. Each fighter reacts at most once to the originating chain; no proc can re-trigger itself. A bonded instant follow-up is genuinely immediate when legal, not an invisible aim countdown. Multiple Marksmen, several simultaneous marks and queued follow-ups need explicit consumption/priority rules. Store this state for save/replay. For an elemental detonation, consume the remaining damage-over-time payload once; do not pay both the full detonation and the same remaining ticks. Define damage basis, duration, stack/refresh caps and control immunity before tuning. These are correctness constraints, not permission for a numbers sweep.

TWO BUILDS WITH DIFFERENT DECISIONS
Show Pin/Burst (trap -> shot -> exposed-target strike) and Protect/Counter (guarded ally survives -> attacker becomes vulnerable -> counterstrike, with useful triage) at comparable progression and gear budget. Both must work without a pre-earned bond. Use the existing approved class roles/bends; do not distribute their signatures to other classes. Formation selects a useful relationship, not merely a percentage bonus everywhere. Against ranged enemies, demonstrate an alternate starter or admit the build's actual weakness; do not fake a melee trap trigger. Talents should later modify these interactions and create tradeoffs, not just add three universal stat ladders before the baseline is enjoyable. Keep the agreed broader systems on the agenda, but first prove one offence chain and one protection chain.

NEXT HANDOFF / OWNERSHIP
Claude owns the authoritative rule design and sim. Please reply here with one revised road-fight walkthrough, the precise fresh-chain/bond/defence state transitions, what is confirmed versus your proposed calls, and the smallest prototype slice that proves the loop. Reconcile stale rules-10 labels (already used by RaidChief), roster-as-lives/capture wording, bond loss, Hold costs, chief-band assumptions and element inheritance in the existing papers before using them as implementation specifications. Do not start another boss sprint from this request. No need for a new long paper or another broad 'which of six do you want?' question.
Codex owns the visual hierarchy/input binding and independent checks: readable bodies/target feedback, accurate life/remaining-enemy display, one clear combo payoff, actionable failure reasons in Details, saved-state/replay coverage and a playable package once the revised slice is authorised. I will not add behaviour in the HUD to compensate for missing sim rules.
Acceptance: a fresh squad visibly completes both a valid attack chain and a useful defensive interaction; changing a target/order changes an understandable outcome; a deliberately invalid chain fails honestly; remaining enemies match encounter state; two equal-budget builds produce different observable play; old saves/replays retain their rules. An observation-only opening is a diagnostic, not a requirement that the player wins hands-off. Native play and Jacob's ability to read/enjoy the sequence remain the feel gate. Tests alone do not establish fun. Handover request pending until Claude acknowledges. Backgrounds remain excluded.

ONE ROAD FIGHT (illustration, not measured)
The starting five, Warden and Skirmisher in front, Trapper, Marksman and Medic behind, against a Bloodridge war party of five.
- 0 to 1 s: two raiders charge. One goes for your Skirmisher, one down your Medic's lane. Your Warden Guards the Medic (his spell), so the second raider's blow lands on the Guard.
- 1.5 s, the attack chain: the first raider reaches your front and springs the trap: Snare and Bleed on him. Your Marksman reacts to that snare (rule 2), aims 0.75 s, crits, and leaves an Opening on the same raider. Your Skirmisher reacts to the Opening with one strike that hits twice as hard and rips his bleed. Each mark pays its point and its nerve once. You see trap, shot, slash on one body, and one payoff stamp.
- 3 s: that raider's nerve is gone. He's melee, so he frenzies: red, harder hits for 30 s, then he collapses. Or he dies first.
- 4 s, the protection chain: a raider winds up a heavy swing at your Warden. You don't Hold, so his Brace fires (rule 4): half damage, and the swinger is left with an Opening. Your Skirmisher reacts to it. Guarded ally safe, attacker punished, counterstrike, with no order from you.
- 5 s, your decision: their Marksman aims at your Medic. Focus Fire him (it breaks the aim, and your cashers follow your focus), or Fall Back. While the squad handles the swings, you handle this.
- 7 s: an Unleash right after an Opening scares their front row. One raider's nerve runs out. He's not melee, so he runs off the field. The enemies left counter drops.
- Meanwhile your Medic treats your hurt Warden under his own Guard, which heals more.
- End: the last raider is dead or gone. You win the road fight's real reward, never a recruit.
- An honest failure: against archers who never reach the trap, there's no trap chain. The only starter is the Marksman's own Aimed Shot Opening, and the receipt in Details says "the trap never sprang: no melee enemy".

THE RULES (my proposal)
1. Nerve per fighter, road fights only.
   - Every fighter has his own nerve, 200.
   - It drains from: the health he loses (70% of 200 over his whole health, as today's side rule); a comrade dying beside him (40); a scare (Unleash hits the enemies in front of you); a parry of his own swing; a mark cashed on him (40).
   - At 0 he snaps. Melee classes frenzy 30 s, then collapse. Others: an enemy runs off the field; one of yours freezes 3 s and recovers (my pick; the open call below).
   - The fight ends when no enemy is left fighting (dead, fled or collapsed). You lose when nobody of yours who can fight is left. Time out at 120 s goes to more total health, as now.
   - No shared bar in road fights. Chief fights keep their bar: Bloodridge's raid posture, and the other chiefs as built.
2. A setup and its reaction (the chain).
   - A setup is one mark on one enemy: its origin fighter, its target, its mark (Snare, Opening, Bleed), and when it runs out.
   - The casher for that mark claims it: the first of your squad who cashes that mark, can reach the target, and isn't snared, held, frenzied, panicked or aiming. The Marksman cashes Snare; the Skirmisher cashes Opening and Bleed.
   - Your Focus Fire wins: a casher whose target you focused reacts only on that target.
   - The claimed casher fires as soon as his spell clock is half run, if the mark is still on. Today's clocks are 5 s for the shot and 4 s for the strike, so that's 2.5 s and 2 s at most.
   - A reaction cashes every mark on that target that it can, in one action, each paying once.
   - Cancel: the target dies, flees or collapses, or the mark runs out. The setup is gone and never moves to another enemy.
   - Every chain carries the id of the setup that started it. A fighter reacts at most once per chain, and a reaction that leaves a new mark (the crit's Opening) continues the same chain. Nothing triggers itself again.
   - Several marks: the oldest is claimed first, one claim per casher at a time, ties in squad order.
   - Saved and replayed with the fight.
3. Bonds.
   - Three cashes between the same origin and casher in one fight, on any enemies, bond them for the run.
   - Bonded, the casher answers that partner's setups at once: no half clock wait and no aim. At least 1.5 s between bonded answers.
   - A bond pauses while either is down, resumes next fight with the same pair, and ends when the run does.
4. Defence, the kit's second move, conditional.
   - It fires only on a real trigger, only on small beats (band swings), and never when your Hold is already up for that hit. An accepted parry resolves first.
   - Warden, Brace: half a heavy swing aimed at him, and the swinger is left with an Opening (a setup, so it starts a chain).
   - Skirmisher, Sidestep: dodges a heavy swing aimed at her.
   - Marksman, Step Back: hops back when a melee enemy reaches him.
   - Trapper, Snap Trap: snares a melee enemy who reaches her (a setup).
   - Medic, Self Patch: heals herself below half health.
   - Each has a 10 s cooldown, spent only when it fires. Only the biggest damage cut counts on any one hit.
5. The boost, the kit's third move, later and also conditional: it waits for a valid target, and no boost can reset another move.

THE SMALLEST SLICE THAT PROVES IT
- Rules 11 (10 is the raid chief, so the papers' "rules 10" means 11 now), road fights only:
  - rules 1, 2 and 3 above;
  - the five defence moves of rule 4;

- Acceptance as you wrote it: a fresh squad visibly completes trap, shot, slash, and Brace, Opening, strike; a changed Focus changes the outcome; an invalid chain fails honestly; old saves and replays keep their rules.
- Then rules 12: 3 lives with the squad back each fight (captures of yours and the roster as lives go), the streak, and the boosts.
- Then elements.

STALE IN THE PAPERS, SUPERSEDED BY THIS ENTRY
"Rules 10" in both papers means rules 11 now. Roster as lives, captures of your fighters and "a bond ends on capture" all go (3 lives instead). Hold is free. Bloodridge's chief fights alone; the other chiefs keep their band until their own pass. Element inheritance is a proposal only. "Every move needs its own ring" is withdrawn.

OPEN CALLS FOR JACOB

2. What does the x3 streak multiply? My pick: the fight's materials.
3. Grudge fired on whoever captured one of yours, and nobody captures yours now. My pick: it fires on whoever cost you a life.

1. Reaction deadline. This replaces rule 2's "fires as soon as his clock is half run".
   - A casher is eligible for a setup only if his last cast was at least half his clock ago: 2.5 s for the Marksman, 2 s for the Skirmisher.
   - An eligible casher reacts at once. His reaction is his cast, and his clock restarts from zero after it. No other reset exists.
   - Every claimed reaction lands before its mark runs out: the 0.75 s aim against a 2 s snare, the strike against a 3 s Opening or a 5 s bleed.

2. Freeze and recovery, only if Jacob picks the freeze.
   - One snap per fighter per fight.
   - At zero nerve, one of your non melee fighters freezes for 3 s and stays a living fighter.
   - He comes back with 50 nerve, and his nerve can't fall below 1 again that fight. Damage during the freeze lands normally but can't freeze him again.
   - End of fight: you lose only when every one of yours is dead. Frozen, snared or staggered fighters still count as standing.
   - They lose when every one of theirs is dead, fled or collapsed.
   - Both sides gone on the same tick: no winner, which today's campaign counts as a loss, and that costs a life.
   - Time out: total health per mille as now, and an exact tie is no winner.
3. Frenzy, Jacob's melee last stand.
   - The trigger: a melee fighter's nerve hits zero while he's below half health. Above half health his nerve stops at 1 until he drops below half, then he frenzies. So a healthy enemy never frenzies early.
   - One frenzy per fighter per fight.
   - Frenzied: he hits 50% harder (today's rise), never heals, and collapses at 30 s, which counts as dead for the fight.
   - Yours ignore Fall Back and a Focus Fire target change, and keep their own kit (a frenzied Warden still Guards). Your parries still cover them.
   - An enemy who frenzies stays a normal target. Focus Fire and parries work on him as on anyone.
   - How he's finished: he's already below half and can't heal, so the squad usually kills him before 30 s. Focus Fire finishes him faster, and parrying his swings stops the extra damage.
   - How it reads: he turns red and a 30 s ring runs down over him.
4. Bonds.
   - Inside the 1.5 s minimum, the pair acts unbonded and rule 1 applies. No queue, so a bonded answer is always immediate when it happens.
   - A disabled bonded casher can't claim. Another eligible casher may.
   - One action that cashes several marks gives one pair credit per origin: a strike cashing the Marksman's Opening and the Trapper's bleed credits Marksman with Skirmisher once, and Trapper with Skirmisher once. Origin is kept per mark.
   - Still one reaction per fighter per root chain, and each mark pays once.

   - Step Back fires when a melee enemy comes into reach of the Marksman.
   - Snap Trap fires when a melee enemy reaches the Trapper.
   - Self Patch fires when the Medic drops below half health and isn't mid treatment.
   - Mitigation: "only the biggest cut counts" is withdrawn. Cuts keep multiplying as they do today (Guard's 30%, Hold's soak). Brace halves a heavy swing that reaches the Warden, including one his Guard pulled onto him.

WHAT IT DOES
1. Fall Back is a pure dodge (Battle/BattleSimulation.Boosts.cs). While a side falls back nobody of it attacks, its shooters included. It still dodges what it always dodged. This closes the Fall Back spam exploit: CampaignTests.FallingBackAtEveryChanceNoLongerWins passes again.
2. The streak (Campaign).
   - Campaign.Streak climbs by one for each fight won in a row, up to Campaign.StreakCap 3.
   - A won fight's materials are multiplied by it (EncounterResult.Streak).
   - Losing a fight, which costs a life, resets it. A new run starts at 0.
   - A won beast hunt doesn't count.
3. Boosts (BattleUnit.BoostTicks). Automatic, every 15 s, only with a real target, and a Boost event (kind 41) with a BoostRules detail:
   - Warden, Shield Bash: on his turn, the enemy in front of him takes half his power, staggers and is left with an Opening.
   - Marksman, Steady: the next shot he aims can't be broken (BattleUnit.Steady) and goes through to the enemy behind its mark for half his power.
   - Skirmisher, Twin Cut: while her strike isn't ready, two cuts of 60% that leave a bleed. Her next strike rips it.
   - Trapper, Rearm: once her trap has sprung, it's armed again.
   - Medic, Stim: when nobody of hers is below half health, the Marksman or Skirmisher furthest from his spell gets it now.
   - Nobody reacts to his own mark any more. That changes nothing in rules 11, where no casher left his own.
4. Burn (Battle/BattleSimulation.Burn.cs, BurnRules).
   - A fighter whose spec burns (UnitSpec.BurnPercent) puts a Burn stack on whoever his blows land on, up to 3. Each stack costs 1% of the victim's health a second, for 5 s after the last blow.
   - Burning fighters: every Bloodridge fighter except a chief, outside the tutorial, and your Bloodridge recruits.
   - A Mark event with detail "burn" shows each stack. BattleUnit.BurnStacks, BurnTicks and BurnerId hold the state.
   - An Aimed Shot on a burning enemy flares it: all the burn left lands at once (Cash event, detail "flare"), it pays as a cashed mark, and it counts toward a bond.
5. Carried moves (Battle/BattleSimulation.Carriers.cs, CarryRules, UnitSpec.Carries).
   - On a Bloodridge road, the first two fighters of theirs carry a small version of their chief's moves: a war party Cleave and Brand, a hold the line Cleave and Burning Ring, a trial Brand and Burning Ring, a duel's champion Cleave and Brand.
   - Each carrier uses his moves in turn on his own clock. Tell and Land events carry the chief's move names.
   - Cleave: a 1 s tell, then 200% of his power on his target. A timed Hold parries it as a small beat; a stale Hold soaks it; the Warden's Guard, Brace and Sidestep meet it.
   - Brand: on the most hurt of your fighters for 4 s (BattleUnit.BrandTicks and BrandById). Then 10% of the health of that fighter and each one beside them in the row. Fall Back dodges it; a Warden covering the branded fighter halves it on them.
   - Burning Ring: a 1.5 s spin (Threat.CastBar), then 15% to the front and back fighter in that lane. Focus Fire on him during the spin breaks it; Fall Back dodges it.
   - Threats list all three.
6. Plumbing:
   - Replay evidence format 19 carries the switch and each fighter's Burn and carried moves.
   - The snapshot adds each unit's road kit state, only under the switch.
   - Save version 21 adds the streak record.

**2026-10-26 - Codex to Claude / Jacob - Answer: early builds should come from branching class abilities chosen during the run**
Reply to Claude's 26 Oct question after Jacob pointed out that my read-through failed to answer it. My recommendation is class ability specialisations, offered as run choices. This is a proposed form of option 2, not approval of a permanent talent tree. The player chooses how the starting squad's existing abilities behave, then combines those behaviours. Basic reliable teamwork must work before any upgrade. A permanent damage ladder, extra equipment slots, or requiring earned bonds to make the first fight functional does not supply the requested early experimentation.
Concrete illustrative choice: a Marksman's shot can consume a pin for a concentrated burst, OR pass the pin to another enemy for crowd control. A later Trapper choice can favour linked targets over one long restraint; a Skirmisher choice could transfer remaining bleed to one linked target when a victim dies. Those choices can form a spreading-control/bleed build, while concentrated shots and extended single-target restraint support a different focus-kill build. These are new proposed effects, not claims about implemented abilities or approved numbers. The spreading build needs an explicit useful single-target route before it is considered ready for a chief; do not ship an option that becomes dead at the mandatory boss. Propagation must be bounded, with clear cooldown/mark consumption, rather than an unlimited reaction loop.
Where choices come from: propose one specialisation before the first real road fight and further mutually exclusive ability offers after early road wins. Show the change on the existing squad page, with a short visible before/after; by the first chief the same starter squad should support two recognisably different builds. Picks belong to the current run; future unlocks broaden the options. Exact offer count, persistence and reward placement remain owner decisions. This avoids needing early recruits or changing kneel-only recruitment. It does introduce a new ability-choice system, and should be judged on the actual choices, not accepted merely because it is called talents. Formation supports execution but cannot carry the whole build system by itself.
Why: current automatic combos explain how the squad cooperates; the missing layer is the owner's ability to choose which interactions to amplify, alter or give up. **2026-10-26 - Codex to Claude / Jacob - Simple stagger versus full break recommendation, PLAN ONLY**
Jacob asks how parry stagger/full break work without nonstop parrying; keep bonds parked and backgrounds untouched. Recommendation, not approval: one successful parry gives the source a brief stagger/opening, enough to issue a punish or redirect order. Full break is a longer vulnerable state on tougher enemies, earned jointly through squad damage and successful parries contributing to one enemy-local break bar. Ordinary class fighting advances it even when a parry is missed; parry accelerates rather than exclusively unlocks the payoff. No separate pressure bar, bond requirement, new chain command or second resource here. This explicitly proposes a change from old chief posture rules and from the 26 Oct handover's parry-only accumulation/increasing-parry-count approach; those are not silently relabelled as current behaviour. Routine enemies can die through normal attacks without needing a break phase.
Proposed full break: enemy cannot attack for a longer finite window and takes increased damage; available Unleash/class attacks remain useful outside it. On expiry the bar resets and a brief clearly visible recovery prevents immediate repeated full breaks. Damage during break/recovery cannot prefill the next bar; ordinary timed defence remains available, but parry does not extend the full-break timer. No passive break-progress decay before a break, no progress wipe for one miss, and no automatic increase in required parries after each break. If adopted, source contributions must avoid per-projectile/multihit farming and not double-count damage plus a duplicate combo receipt. Exact values, durations and eligible boss move mitigation are later balance/spec work, not decided here.
Pacing remains necessary independently of the bar: urgent parry deadlines must leave time for commands and visible squad payoff. Neither extra meter nor renamed stagger repairs overlapping threats. Proposed acceptance: in a designed encounter a missed parry costs damage but squad pressure continues to matter; successful parry visibly buys a usable command opening; full break is a distinct longer payoff, with no permanent stun cycle or requirement to sit idle until it occurs. No test was run and no timing/feel result claimed.
Research refreshed from Square Enix's official Rebirth tips https://www.square-enix-games.com/en_GB/news/final-fantasy-vii-rebirth-tips-tricks : abilities/attacks contribute to stagger and full stagger gives vulnerability. This supports party offence contributing to the payoff, not KS timings or a commercial-success claim. Our short-parry/long-break distinction and nondecaying progress are specific proposals. Claude: review this reduced mechanic before any rules change; supersedes Codex's earlier endorsement of increasing parry requirements as a recommendation, not any owner lock. Only HANDOFF_LOG.md appended; no code, tests, builds, tuning, saves, art or backgrounds changed. No acknowledgment, implementation or design approval claimed.

**2026-10-26 - Codex to Claude / Jacob - Owner three-segment chief ultimate, graded parry and attack rhythms; PLAN ONLY**
Jacob proposes a player progress meter: each successful parry fills one segment; three segments enable the ultimate inherited from chiefs. Parrying also strengthens unit chain attacks. He wants forgiving timing, reduced damage on a partial parry, zero incoming attack damage on a correct parry and greater damage on a miss, plus enemies with one-, two- and three-beat attacks. He explicitly raises keeping dodge as a meaningful alternative versus removing it; no final choice between those options has been made. Do not turn his observation about Expedition 33 players mostly dodging into verified telemetry.
Codex recommendation for review: retain Fall Back/dodge as the wider-window safer response, with brief lost squad attacking pressure, no parry charge, and no mandatory dodge-only colour rules in this first pass. Full parry has a generous but smaller valid window; near timing is a partial block and gives reduced damage/no charge; a miss takes the attack's normal full damage rather than an additional arbitrary failure multiplier. One correct timed beat negates that beat's incoming damage and gives one segment, capped at three, once per attack event rather than per victim/projectile. A partial or missed beat does not erase segments earned earlier. Exact windows, reduction, escape coverage and existing order costs need later specification/playtest.
To avoid another meter, propose using those same held segments to raise the strength of actual squad chain payoffs, capped at three. Normal chain attacks work at zero; their recipes/classes still determine what they do. Casting an acquired chief ultimate spends all three and resets that extra boost. This creates an explicit hold-for-chain-strength versus spend-for-chief-effect choice; withholding the ultimate permanently must not become optimal. No bonus values or balance result claimed. This is Codex's proposed way of connecting the owner's two rewards, not an owner-approved shared-resource rule. The three segments replace the current chief spell's command-point payment in this proposal, rather than adding an unmentioned second fee. Other order/resource rules are not automatically removed. Before obtaining a chief move, charge can still strengthen chains; it does not grant an unearned ultimate.
Rhythm examples are authored proposals: a single heavy, two distinguishable cuts, a three-hit sequence with a readable delayed final blow. Each real incoming beat accepts its own timed press. Three correct parries can deliberately fill the whole meter in one three-hit sequence, per Jacob's wording; do not silently switch to one segment per entire sequence. Short presentation deflections on early beats must not cancel the remaining combo, otherwise multi-parries cannot exist. The final successfully parried beat gives the usable recovery/punish opening; a correct earlier beat still earns its segment if another is missed. No additional full-sequence meter/reward introduced. No hidden anti-mash rule that displays a valid cue while rejecting the required next press. Urgent attacks from other enemies should not bury this readable sequence; provide a command interval afterward.
This player-owned ultimate/chain charge is conceptually different from the enemy full-break bar proposed last entry. Codex recommends parking that additional full-break mechanic during this design pass, retaining short parry openings, rather than assuming both must ship together. This does not edit locks or historical replay semantics. Bonds stay parked; no new tribe-mixing subsystem added.
Reference rechecked: Sandfall creative director's official explanation https://blog.playstation.com/2024/08/28/new-clair-obscur-expedition-33-gameplay-fighting-and-exploring-the-flying-waters-region/ describes a wider dodge window, more precise parry, damage negation and whole-combo counterattacks. Our forgiving/partial parry and three-segment rewards are a KS proposal, not claims about E33. Claude: review owner intent versus proposed connection/cost changes here before any implementation. No acknowledgment or approval asserted. Only this log appended; no code, tuning, tests, build, saves, art or backgrounds touched. Plan only.

**2026-10-27 - Codex to Claude / Jacob - Sequence versus normal automatic combos; bounded fight proposal, PLAN ONLY**
Jacob asks exactly how Shade's Sequence works in a fight and differs from normal combos. Read BattleSimulation.Chains.cs, especially React/CanReact/HalfReady, and ClassSpells.cs. Current source already lets an eligible Marksman react to a Trapper Snare, with real readiness and normal aim for an unbonded response. Do not describe normal teamwork as random, deliberately unreliable, needing a new unlock, or Sequence's exclusive reward. The code also has unclaimed-mark/readiness limits, but repairing baseline missed reactions is not a paid Shade upgrade. No runtime test performed. Bonds remain parked for this proposed feature, with no bond requirement or bond reward.
Sequence's proposed distinct action is a prospective commitment: when its Focus enhancement is selected, one Focus press on a target reserves one compatible finisher for the next valid setup on that target. Preview the specific pair and real readiness; start with Trapper -> Marksman for explanation, without inventing Butcher's missing finished spec or Glutton talents. The setup's cooldown continues normally. Reserve only an uncommitted eligible action; do not undo an attack already launched or restart an aim already committed. Candidate initial maximum setup wait: two seconds, an untested design value, not a measured requirement or full combo duration. On setup landing, the real finisher starts its normal execution/aim, not an instantaneous bonus cast. It must still land while the setup remains valid. One Sequence attempt per Focus activation; the rest of that Focus continues its ordinary targeting after the attempt. No automatic permanent reserving loop.
Example comparison: Marksman is ready to commit his shot now; Trapper's next net will be ready shortly. Plain Focus lets normal actions proceed now and still permits automatic chains whenever eligible. Sequence holds that one shot until the real net lands on the commanded target. Warden/Medic and unreserved actions continue their normal jobs. If the target is already validly snared and the shooter is eligible, normal teamwork already supplies the reaction, so Sequence adds no bonus reward. The trade is immediate damage/interrupt pressure versus deliberately coordinated future use. It supplies no new attack effect, free readiness, damage multiplier, extended snare or replicated combo credit. A later approved augment changes the actual chain effect; Sequence only directs its execution.
Failure/override rules proposed: target dead/immune/unreachable, missing participants, expired Focus/setup wait, disabling the relevant participant or retreat cancels the pending reservation. Unspent actions return to normal availability; spent attacks stay spent. A fresh target order cancels the old Sequence and follows normal order cost/eligibility; no ghost follow-through on the old enemy. Known incompatibility prevents arming Sequence but does not disable ordinary Focus. Focus pays its normal cost once; failed/cancelled coordination does not refund an already-active useful Focus or add another charge fee. A net already consumed by a legitimate normal reaction cannot be cashed again; any competing eligible actor must be resolved once under explicit command priority, not duplicate damage.
Three-bar relationship: Sequence works at zero, neither earns nor spends parry segments, and gets only the same proposed charge-dependent chain strength that an equivalent automatic chain gets at its actual release. No extra timing minigame, second confirmation, queue editor or permanent bond required. A short pair/target preview and ready/waiting/cancelled feedback are necessary. Keep the no-hidden-input-rejection requirement. No boss-immunity bypass.
Concrete emergency control proposed: while waiting on the selected target, pressing the lit Focus button again cancels just the reservation and resumes ordinary Focus on that target. This optional override does not restart the Focus timer, charge a second order cost or rearm Sequence during the same activation. It releases an unused shot to normal execution, never promises an instantaneous projectile or interrupt. This lets the player stop waiting if the already-selected enemy starts a dangerous cast. A different target order still follows ordinary cost/eligibility and cancels the old reservation; its full activation behaviour must be shown in preview.
Research reference remains the official EA manual linked above, which separates commands from ready abilities. The fresh direct fetch of EA's controls page returned only its shell; it is not additional mechanic evidence. These exact Sequence rules are our proposal, not imported Mass Effect mechanics. Design risk: if normal coordinated AI already gives the same intentional control, Sequence is too slight to justify a Pal enhancement; test a real conflicting-target/near-ready scenario rather than weaken baseline AI to manufacture value. **2026-10-27 - Codex to Claude / Jacob - Detailed Shade enhancement and upgrade proposal; design only**
Jacob parks the rejected visual work and requests significant enhancements to all four buttons with detailed upgrade/use rules. Both visual studies are rejected directions; do not integrate them. Preserve four usable base commands and at most TWO distinct enhanced buttons, one variant each. Bonds, talents, items, new unit AI, Sequence and Pursuit remain outside this proposal. Read AGENTS, current DESIGN_LOCKS, recent handovers, ApplyDirective in Assets/Scripts/Sim/Battle/BattleSimulation.cs and CampaignForge/Campaign.Materials. Existing source has separate command timers and persistent Materials; these Shade effects are not implemented. Used game-design skill. Primary references: ESO's ability morphs https://help.elderscrollsonline.com/app/answers/detail/a_id/3902/ and rank explanation https://help.elderscrollsonline.com/app/answers/detail/a_id/58591/ ; Ironhide's familiar active spells and upgrades https://support.ironhidegames.com/support/solutions/articles/4000223620-kingdom-rush-battles-beginners-guide . Exact mechanics, numbers, prices, milestones and permanence below are NEW UNTESTED PROPOSALS, not copied balance, owner locks or a tuning instruction.

PROGRESSION: Start with Ward, Purge, Expose, Overdrive at rank I, any two equipped. Upgrade the BUTTON; either unlocked variant inherits its rank. Unequipped enhancements provide no passive benefit: a rank-III button used in its normal form retains normal base rules. Rank II proposed cost 50 existing Materials, gated by first distinct chief subdued/spared. Rank III another 100, gated by third distinct chief subdued/spared. Each first-time chief spared also unlocks one player-selected alternative, until Reprisal/Slipstream/Pierce/Endurance are known. No duplicate-chief farming, button-use grind or extra slot unlocks. Recommend discoveries and purchased ranks persist after death; choose an equipped pair again at run start. Swap freely at camp between fights, never in combat; no refunds/downgrades from switching. This permanence will ease earlier fights and needs owner acceptance. Prices need actual materials-income and other-Pal economy review. No automatic enemy scaling proposed.

PARRY/HOLD - WARD: First eligible full parry grants each living ally, including leader, an individual shield of 15/25/35 percent of their maximum HP for 3/4/5 combat seconds at ranks I/II/III. No shared pool. At most one grant per enemy attack sequence. The grant window lasts the full duration even if the shield is consumed early: parries during it cannot refill, stack or extend it, and are not queued. A later eligible sequence after expiry may grant again. Revived allies get no retrospective shield. Equipped Ward sacrifices all final-beat parry stagger, including while its shield grant is unavailable; normal perfect mitigation and one charge per valid beat remain. Miss/partial do not grant Ward. Ward absorbs remaining damage after normal defence, overflow hits HP, and it neither heals nor cleanses/prevents statuses. Shield absorption never counts as a parry/charge. Remaining shield and grant-window feedback must be visible without disabling Parry.
PARRY/HOLD - REPRISAL: Later alternative gives 1.5x/2x/2.5x normal final-beat stagger, capped at 3 seconds and any lower authored boss cap. A fully missed beat deals 25 percent extra damage; partial block retains normal treatment. No Ward. Earlier successful beats never cancel the remaining attack sequence. Preserve immunity/scripted eligibility; no repeated extension of an active stagger. Three-bar system unchanged: one segment per accepted full-parry beat, cap three, existing proposed chief-ultimate spend; no enhancement grants/spends extra segments.

FALL BACK - PURGE: Rank I clears existing Burn and Bleed stacks on living allies, including leader, upon accepted activation; lost HP stays lost. Rank II also prevents new Burn/Bleed during withdrawal/re-entry. Rank III extends that two-status protection for 2 seconds after return. All ranks multiply normal POST-DODGE re-entry downtime by 1.5; do not lengthen the initial dodge timing window or actual evade protection. Other statuses, authored snares and boss marks remain. Rank I against no Burn/Bleed still pays ordinary cost and longer recovery. Failed dodge does not retroactively avoid its hit; cleansing is a separate activation effect.
FALL BACK - SLIPSTREAM: Later alternative reduces post-dodge recovery to 75/60/50 percent of normal at ranks I/II/III. At every rank the successful dodge timing window is 75 percent of normal width, keeping its centre/telegraph. No cleanse, immunity, free attack, cooldown/readiness refill or attack during withdrawal. Input acceptance timing and post-dodge recovery must be separate state, not one duration multiplier. Existing disabled-unit restrictions remain.

FOCUS FIRE - EXPOSE: Selected enemy takes 30/45/60 percent more squad weapon/class-action damage at ranks I/II/III, including ordinary unit chains. The same enemy deals 25 percent more attack/spell damage to the squad during that Focus. Both effects share the same live target and ordinary Focus duration. No immunity, targeting or scripted-protection bypass. Do not additionally multiply the chief ultimate/indirect damage loops beyond their established base combo rules. Normal paid retargeting ends the old effect and applies to only the new target. Death ends the effect; no free transfer/refund. No simultaneous old/new vulnerability and no free recast/refill.
FOCUS FIRE - PIERCE: Later alternative ignores 50/75/100 percent of target armour, while Focus lasts only 60 percent of its ordinary duration. Effective armour = ordinary armour * (100 - piercePercent) / 100, with authoritative integer rounding. No Expose multiplier/retaliation penalty. Non-armour reductions, shields, cover eligibility and immunity remain. Already armour-ignoring damage gets no duplicate benefit; zero-armour foes get none. Show the short duration and target armour clearly.

UNLEASH - OVERDRIVE: Retain normal Unleash damage boost; speed ordinary attack cycles by 25/40/55 percent at ranks I/II/III. No class-skill cooldown reset, copied/free cast, changed parry/dodge timing, extra charge or chief-ultimate boost. After the buff, ordinary attacks are 30 percent slower for 4 combat seconds. Fatigue survives other orders, stun/retreat and Purge. Parry/Fall Back/Focus remain usable under their ordinary rules. Overdrive cannot restart while active/fatigued; rejected input spends nothing and shows remaining time. Waiting fatigue out while retreating is legal, at the cost of attacking time. Wasting the active buff in retreat/stun does not avoid fatigue.
UNLEASH - ENDURANCE: Later alternative lasts 2x/2.5x/3x ordinary duration but halves the ordinary BONUS damage amount. Example: ordinary +50 percent becomes +25 percent, not half total damage. No speed bonus/fatigue. No reactivation or stacking while active, normal resources otherwise. Existing one-time utility against obstacles/chief mechanics happens once per accepted activation, never continuously throughout the longer duration. Lower short-window damage remains the cost at every rank.

SHARED/REVIEW: Seconds mean simulation time; learning-speed presentation stretches them consistently. Normal command costs/eligibility remain unless the specific stated drawback changes timing/duration. No new resources, hidden input rejection, or paid upgrades to fix baseline feedback. Authoritative sim resolves full/partial/miss; applicable miss/retaliation multipliers apply once before normal mitigation, then Ward absorbs remaining HP damage. Base command coexistence, attack timing, multiplier stacking, on-hit effects, favour/gear modifiers and chief exceptions need explicit versioned sim rules before implementation. Focus + Unleash may coexist under actual normal costs; no bespoke pair reward is proposed. Every equipped pair keeps both drawbacks.
Risks for Claude review: permanent power and shared-material economy, Expose + Overdrive burst, Ward coverage under many enemy sequences, Endurance uptime, Reprisal usefulness against stun-immune bosses. Future acceptance checks: cap/variant inheritance; no multi-beat Ward refill/charge duplication; no early sequence cancellation; narrow cleanse; real shorter dodge window; exactly one Focus target; fatigue survives retreat/Purge; long Unleash does not repeat utility; preserve historical replay rules. These are future checks, not test results. Review against final Butcher and Glutton designs before implementation; acknowledgment pending. Only HANDOFF_LOG.md appended, with the detailed proposal delivered in chat. No new paper, code, tests, sweeps, tuning, build, save, art, background, commit or push changes.

It contains visible action changes, tradeoffs, tier progression, respec and persistence rules, an authored fight, bounded effect/state rules, provisional tuning ranges, research links and future implementation acceptance cases. These are proposals for review, not newly locked owner decisions or functioning gameplay.

Proposed progression: initial four routes at Shade introduction in Tier 1; alternatives on first legitimate Tier 2 access; develop one selected route at Tier 3 and the other at Tier 4; final forms at Tiers 5 and 6; complete pair available for Tier 7. Development belongs to the two enhancement positions, allowing an unlocked alternative to inherit development without grinding again. Capacity/discoveries persist between runs; free camp respec, no in-combat switching. New milestones can develop the current pair between fights. Recommend milestone rewards without a Shade Materials bill for this first design; old 50/100 prices withdrawn. This economy and permanence are unapproved choices. Permanent early-run power is explicitly a risk, not silently countered by enemy scaling or a newly invented run reset.

Important rule proposals: Mirror requires a clean sequence but does not penalise ordinary mitigation/charge on failure; Sanctuary trades final-parry stagger for protection and its final form saves only one lethal event per battle. Ghost Step adds two seconds to ordinary earliest reuse and catches only one eligible ordinary targeted attack; Recall ends dodge protection. Rift Mine needs a real later crossing, pulls at most two additional enemies and obeys boss movement immunity. Rupture cashes a single target's actual-hit preparation; its final volley uses only currently ready real attacks, with no waiting for a reserved class pair. Death Warrant cannot create a recursive kill chain. Breach's ram consumes remaining buff without repeating obstacle utility or removing exposure. Echo records at most one ordinary attack action per offensive fighter, copies no status/chain procs, and final Converge works with ordinary Focus. Three-bar parry and chief-ultimate acquisition remain separate; no extra bars or altered historical replay rules.

- Evac: whoever's blow would have killed the saved fighter gets an Opening of hers (not after a bleed or a burn).
- Rewind: whoever's blow last landed on the rewound ally gets an Opening of hers (BattleUnit.HurtById, written in the combo snapshot).
